**→ Write**

`~\finn\backend\tests\test_margins.py`

```
"""Margin-comparison precision: quarterly margin comparisons are decided on exact margins, never on screener's
whole-number OPM %, and a comparison with only rounded figures is 'unverifiable'.

The TATATECH case is the row the production rebuild of 2026-11-09 produced: Q4 FY26 and Q2 FY26 both read "16%",
so the model called "EBITDA margins that exceed our Q2 run-rate" missed. From screener's own statement rows the exact
margins are 252 / 1,572 = 16.03% and 208 / 1,323 = 15.72%, so the promise was delivered.
"""
import copy
import importlib.util
import pathlib

import pytest

from finn.pull import financials, ledger, periods

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent

# TATATECH consolidated quarterly rows (screener.in), the quarters this promise involves.
TATATECH_Q = {"Sep 2025": (1323.0, 208.0, 16.0, 166.0), "Dec 2025": (1366.0, 193.0, 14.0, 7.0),
              "Mar 2026": (1572.0, 252.0, 16.0, 204.0)}  # sales, operating profit, OPM % (rounded), net profit

GUIDANCE = {"id": "G2.2", "call": "Q3 FY26", "subject": "EBITDA margin", "target": "exceed our Q2 run-rate",
            "horizon": "Q4", "period": "Q4 FY26",
            "statement": "For Q4, we expect sequential revenue growth in excess of 10%, and despite the impacts of new "
                         "labour codes, deliver EBITDA Margins that exceed our Q2 run-rate."}

# The row exactly as the 2026-11-09 production rebuild returned it.
REBUILT_ROW = {"subject": "Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin exceed Q2 run‑rate", "promise": "EBITDA margins exceed Q2 run‑rate for Q4 FY26",
               "verdict": "missed", "guidance_ids": ["G2.2"], "fact_ids": ["Q.OPM %.Mar 2026", "Q.OPM %.Sep 2025"],
               "why": "Margin did not exceed the Q2 run‑rate", "delivered": "Q4 margin 16% equals Q2 margin 16%"}


def _company(q: dict):
    cols = list(q)
    col = lambda i: [v[i] for v in q.values()]  # noqa: E731
    rows = {"Sales": col(0), "Operating Profit": col(1), "OPM %": col(2), "Net Profit": col(3),
            "Profit before tax": [round(v * 1.3, 1) for v in col(3)]}
    return {"symbol": "TATATECH", "basis": "consolidated", "name": "Tata Technologies", "about": None, "bse_code": None,
            "sector": None, "top": {}, "url": "https://example.invalid", "concalls": [], "annual_reports": [],
            "tables": {"quarters": {"cols": cols, "rows": rows}, "annual": None, "balance": None, "cashflow": None,
                       "ratios": None, "shareholding": None}}


def _facts(monkeypatch, q=TATATECH_Q) -> dict:
    monkeypatch.setattr(financials.screener, "company", lambda sym: _company(q))
    return financials.build("TATATECH")["facts"]


def _guard(row: dict, facts: dict, latest: str = "Sep 2026") -> dict:
    """The ledger's post-model guards, in build() order."""
    r = copy.deepcopy(row)
    guidance = {GUIDANCE["id"]: GUIDANCE}
    ledger._metric_guard(r, facts)
    ledger._period_guard(r, guidance, facts, periods.from_calendar(latest))
    ledger._margin_guard(r, guidance, facts)
    ledger._range_check(r, guidance, facts)
    ledger._horizon_guard(r, guidance, latest)
    return r


# ---------- the exact TATATECH case ----------

def test_tatatech_exact_margins_differ_where_rounded_opm_ties(monkeypatch):
    F = _facts(monkeypatch)
    assert F["Q.OPM %.Mar 2026"]["value"] == F["Q.OPM %.Sep 2025"]["value"] == 16.0      # screener: a tie
    assert F["calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Mar 2026"]["value"] == 16.03                           # 252 / 1,572
    assert F["calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Sep 2025"]["value"] == 15.72                           # 208 / 1,323


def test_tatatech_q4_fy26_margin_vs_q2_run_rate_is_delivered_on_exact_margins(monkeypatch):
    r = _guard(REBUILT_ROW, _facts(monkeypatch))
    assert r["verdict"] == "delivered" and r["downgraded_from"] == "missed"
    assert r["fact_ids"] == ["calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Mar 2026", "calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Sep 2025"]
    assert r["replaced_fact_ids"] == ["Q.OPM %.Mar 2026", "Q.OPM %.Sep 2025"]
    assert r["margin_check"] == {"result": "above",
                                 "target": {"period": "Q4 FY26", "value": 16.03, "fact": "calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Mar 2026"},
                                 "base": {"period": "Q2 FY26", "value": 15.72, "fact": "calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Sep 2025"}}
    assert "16.03% in Q4 FY26" in r["why"] and "15.72% in Q2 FY26" in r["why"]
    assert "period_check" not in r  # the right quarters were cited; only the precision was wrong


def test_exact_margin_not_above_the_base_is_missed(monkeypatch):
    lower = {**TATATECH_Q, "Mar 2026": (1572.0, 243.7, 16.0, 204.0)}  # 15.50%: still "16%" rounded, but below 15.72%
    r = _guard({**REBUILT_ROW, "verdict": "delivered"}, _facts(monkeypatch, lower))
    assert r["verdict"] == "missed" and r["downgraded_from"] == "delivered"
    assert r["margin_check"]["result"] == "not_above" and "15.5% in Q4 FY26" in r["why"]


def test_correct_model_verdict_is_kept_with_exact_figures(monkeypatch):
    r = _guard({**REBUILT_ROW, "verdict": "delivered", "why": "Model's own reason"}, _facts(monkeypatch))
    assert r["verdict"] == "delivered" and "downgraded_from" not in r and r["why"] == "Model's own reason"
    assert r["fact_ids"] == ["calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Mar 2026", "calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Sep 2025"]


# ---------- rounded ties without exact figures ----------

ROUNDED_ONLY = {fid: {"id": fid, "label": "OPM %", "value": 16.0, "unit": "%", "period": fid.split(".", 2)[2]}
                for fid in ("Q.OPM %.Mar 2026", "Q.OPM %.Sep 2025")}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("model_said", ["missed", "delivered", "on_track", "at_risk"])
def test_rounded_tie_without_exact_margins_is_unverifiable(model_said):
    r = _guard({**REBUILT_ROW, "verdict": model_said}, ROUNDED_ONLY)
    assert r["verdict"] == "unverifiable" and r["downgraded_from"] == model_said
    assert r["why"] == "Only rounded margins are available (16% in Q4 FY26 vs 16% in Q2 FY26), and they can't settle a margin comparison."
    assert r["margin_check"] == {"result": "rounded_only", "quarters": ["Q2 FY26", "Q4 FY26"]}


def test_exact_figure_for_only_one_quarter_is_not_mixed_with_a_rounded_one():
    facts = {**ROUNDED_ONLY, "calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Mar 2026": {"id": "calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Mar 2026", "label": "EBITDA margin",
                                                               "value": 16.03, "unit": "%", "period": "Mar 2026"}}
    r = _guard(REBUILT_ROW, facts)
    assert r["verdict"] == "unverifiable" and r["fact_ids"] == REBUILT_ROW["fact_ids"]


def test_exchange_filing_margins_count_as_exact():
    x = {f"X.EBITDA margin.{q}": {"id": f"X.EBITDA margin.{q}", "label": "EBITDA margin (exchange filing)", "value": v,
                                  "unit": "%", "period": q} for q, v in (("Q4 FY26", 16.0), ("Q2 FY26", 15.7))}
    r = _guard(REBUILT_ROW, {**ROUNDED_ONLY, **x})
    assert r["verdict"] == "delivered" and r["fact_ids"] == ["X.EBITDA margin.Q4 FY26", "X.EBITDA margin.Q2 FY26"]


# ---------- rows the guard must leave alone ----------

def test_single_quarter_margin_is_made_exact_without_changing_the_verdict(monkeypatch):
    row = {**REBUILT_ROW, "verdict": "at_risk", "why": "unchanged", "fact_ids": ["Q.OPM %.Mar 2026"]}
    r = ledger._margin_guard(row := copy.deepcopy(row), {"G2.2": GUIDANCE}, _facts(monkeypatch)) or row
    assert r["verdict"] == "at_risk" and r["why"] == "unchanged" and r["fact_ids"] == ["calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Mar 2026"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("verdict", ["too_early", "unverifiable", "goalposts_moved", "dropped"])
def test_non_outcome_verdicts_are_not_decided_by_the_margin_guard(verdict):
    row = {**REBUILT_ROW, "verdict": verdict}
    ledger._margin_guard(row, {"G2.2": GUIDANCE}, ROUNDED_ONLY)
    assert row["verdict"] == verdict and "margin_check" not in row


def test_lender_margins_are_not_touched():
    pp = {f"X.Pre-provision margin.{q}": {"id": f"X.Pre-provision margin.{q}", "label": "Pre-provision margin (exchange filing)",
                                          "value": v, "unit": "%", "period": q} for q, v in (("Q2 FY26", 3.1), ("Q2 FY27", 3.0))}
    row = {**REBUILT_ROW, "verdict": "at_risk", "fact_ids": list(pp)}
    ledger._margin_guard(row, {"G2.2": GUIDANCE}, pp)
    assert row["verdict"] == "at_risk" and row["fact_ids"] == list(pp) and "margin_check" not in row


# ---------- what the model sees, and the whole build ----------

def test_ledger_input_hides_rounded_opm_where_an_exact_margin_exists(monkeypatch):
    F = _facts(monkeypatch)
    F["Q.OPM %.Jun 2025"] = {"id": "Q.OPM %.Jun 2025", "label": "OPM %", "value": 15.0, "unit": "%", "period": "Jun 2025"}
    text, ids = ledger._actuals_text(F)
    assert "calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Mar 2026 = 16.03% [Q4 FY26]" in text and "calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Sep 2025 = 15.72%" in text
    assert "Q.OPM %.Mar 2026" not in ids and "Q.OPM %.Sep 2025" not in ids
    assert "Q.OPM %.Jun 2025" in ids  # no exact margin for that quarter: the rounded one stays
    assert "never decide a comparison on it" in ledger.SYSTEM


def test_ledger_build_end_to_end_decides_the_tatatech_row_on_exact_margins(monkeypatch):
    F = _facts(monkeypatch)
    rev = {"id": "G2.1", "call": "Q3 FY26", "subject": "sequential revenue growth", "target": "in excess of 10%",
           "horizon": "Q4", "period": "Q4 FY26", "statement": GUIDANCE["statement"]}
    calls = [{"call": "Q3 FY26", "guidance": [rev, GUIDANCE]}]
    first = {**REBUILT_ROW, "delivered": "Margin did not exceed the Q2 run-rate"}  # cites the (now hidden) rounded ids
    second = {**first, "fact_ids": ["calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Mar 2026", "calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Sep 2025"]}
    prompts = []

    def fake_chat_json(tag, tier, system, user, max_tokens):
        prompts.append(user)
        return {"rows": [copy.deepcopy(first if len(prompts) == 1 else second)], "credibility": "ok"}

    monkeypatch.setattr(ledger, "chat_json", fake_chat_json)
    out = ledger.build(calls, F, "Mar 2026")
    row = out["rows"][0]
    assert "unknown fact ids ['Q.OPM %.Mar 2026', 'Q.OPM %.Sep 2025']" in prompts[1]  # rounded ids are not citable
    assert row["verdict"] == "delivered" and row["downgraded_from"] == "missed"
    assert [f["value"] for f in row["facts"]] == [16.03, 15.72]


# ---------- the production audit ----------

def test_audit_flags_rounded_margin_comparison_and_passes_the_guarded_row(monkeypatch):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("audit_periods", HERE.parent.parent / "scripts" / "audit_periods.py")
    audit = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(audit)
    F = _facts(monkeypatch)

    def memo(row):
        stored = {**row, "evidence": [GUIDANCE], "facts": [F[f] for f in row["fact_ids"]]}
        return {"sections": {"trajectory": {"quarterly": [{"period": "Sep 2026"}]}, "ledger": {"rows": [stored]}}}

    _, before = audit.audit_memo(memo(REBUILT_ROW))
    assert [f["problem"] for f in before] == [
        "Margin comparison of Q2 FY26, Q4 FY26 decided on rounded OPM % (Q.OPM %.Mar 2026, Q.OPM %.Sep 2025); exact margins are needed."]
    _, after = audit.audit_memo(memo(_guard(REBUILT_ROW, F)))
    assert not [f for f in after if f["problem"]]

```

`~\finn\backend\finn\pull\narrative.py`

```
"""Deterministic consistency checks on the memo's model-written prose.

The ledger and thesis models write sentences; the ledger's code guards then fix verdicts. Nothing made the prose agree
with the fixed verdicts or with the figures a sentence cites. These checks do, without a model call:

  - comparison wording: "sequential(ly)" / "quarter-on-quarter" must rest on adjacent quarters, "year-on-year" on the
    same quarter a year apart (Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26 is year-on-year, never sequential);
  - promise status: a point may say a promise is met / validated / delivered only if every promise it cites is
    "delivered" in the ledger — a "too_early" promise (e.g. H2 FY27, not started) has not been tested;
  - the ledger's credibility summary: "missed X" / "hit X" must match X's final verdict, else FINN writes the summary
    from the verdicts themselves.
"""
import re

from . import periods

# ---------- comparison wording ----------

_SEQUENTIAL = re.compile(r"\bsequential(?:ly)?\b|\bquarter[- ]on[- ]quarter\b|\bq-?o-?q\b|\bfrom the (?:previous|prior|preceding) quarter\b", re.I)
_YEAR_ON_YEAR = re.compile(r"\byear[- ]on[- ]year\b|\by-?o-?y\b|\bfrom a year (?:earlier|ago)\b", re.I)


def _quarterly_pairs(evidence: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[tuple], list[tuple]]:
    """(adjacent pairs, year-apart pairs) among the cited quarterly figures, per metric."""
    by_metric: dict[str, set] = {}
    for e in evidence:
        fid = str(e.get("id") or "")
        if e.get("type") != "fact" or "value" not in e or "." not in fid:
            continue
        p = periods.fact_period(fid, e.get("period"))
        if p and p.kind == "quarter":
            by_metric.setdefault(fid.rsplit(".", 1)[0], set()).add(p.start)
    adjacent, year_apart = [], []
    for metric, qs in by_metric.items():
        for a in qs:
            for b in qs:
                if b == a.shift(1):
                    adjacent.append((metric, a, b))
                if b == a.shift(4):
                    year_apart.append((metric, a, b))
    return adjacent, year_apart


def comparison_issue(point: str, evidence: list[dict]) -> str | None:
    adjacent, year_apart = _quarterly_pairs(evidence)
    if _SEQUENTIAL.search(point) and year_apart and not adjacent:
        _, a, b = year_apart[0]
        return f"Calls a {b.label} vs {a.label} comparison sequential; the same quarter a year apart is year-on-year."
    if _YEAR_ON_YEAR.search(point) and adjacent and not year_apart:
        _, a, b = adjacent[0]
        return f"Calls a {b.label} vs {a.label} comparison year-on-year; adjacent quarters are sequential."
    return None


# ---------- promise status ----------

_ACHIEVED = (r"(?:validat|vindicat|deliver|achiev|fulfil|honou?r|confirm|meet|met\b|kept\b|keep|hit\b|beat)\w*")
_PROMISE = r"(?:promise|guidance|target|goal|commitment|pledge)s?"
_CLAIMS_ACHIEVED = re.compile(rf"\b{_ACHIEVED}\s+(?:[\w'’‑-]+\s+){{0,5}}?{_PROMISE}\b|\b{_PROMISE}\s+(?:[\w'’‑-]+\s+){{0,4}}?(?:was\s+|were\s+|is\s+|has been\s+|been\s+)?{_ACHIEVED}", re.I)
_NEGATED = re.compile(r"\b(?:not|never|no|yet to|fail\w*|short of|without|cannot|can't|can’t)\s+(?:\w+\s+){0,2}$", re.I)
_STATUS = {"too_early": "too early to judge", "unverifiable": "not verifiable from the sources", "missed": "missed",
           "at_risk": "at risk", "on_track": "on track but not yet delivered", "dropped": "dropped",
           "goalposts_moved": "softened or pushed out"}


def _claims_achievement(point: str) -> bool:
    return any(not _NEGATED.search(point[:m.start()]) for m in _CLAIMS_ACHIEVED.finditer(point))


def _cited_promises(refs: list[str], ledger_rows: dict[str, dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """Ledger rows a point cites: directly (L3) or through a guidance item a row is built on (G5.2)."""
    rows = [ledger_rows[r] for r in refs if r in ledger_rows]
    rows += [row for row in ledger_rows.values() if set(refs) & set(row.get("guidance_ids") or []) and row not in rows]
    return rows


def promise_issue(point: str, refs: list[str], evidence: list[dict], ledger_rows: dict[str, dict],
                  latest: periods.FQ | None) -> str | None:
    if not _claims_achievement(point):
        return None
    for row in _cited_promises(refs, ledger_rows):
        if row.get("verdict") != "delivered":
            p = periods.latest_promise(row.get("evidence") or [])
            when = f" ({p.label} hasn't started)" if p and latest and p.start > latest else ""
            return (f"Says a promise is met, but the ledger marks '{row.get('subject')}' "
                    f"{_STATUS.get(row.get('verdict'), row.get('verdict'))}{when}.")
    for e in evidence:  # a cited guidance item about a period that hasn't started, even with no ledger row
        if e.get("type") == "guidance" and latest and (p := periods.promise_period(e)) and p.start > latest:
            return f"Says a promise is met, but the promise is about {p.label}, which hasn't started."
    return None


def thesis_issues(thesis: dict, ledger: dict, latest: periods.FQ | None) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """{"bull2": {"supported": False, "issue": "…"}} for every bull/bear point that fails a check."""
    led = {f"L{i + 1}": r for i, r in enumerate(ledger.get("rows", []))}
    out = {}
    for side in ("bull", "bear"):
        for i, p in enumerate(thesis.get(side) or []):
            ev = p.get("evidence") or []
            if issue := comparison_issue(p["point"], ev) or promise_issue(p["point"], p.get("refs") or [], ev, led, latest):
                out[f"{side}{i + 1}"] = {"supported": False, "issue": issue}
    return out


# ---------- credibility summary ----------

_OUTCOME_WORDS = {
    "missed": re.compile(r"\bmiss(?:ed|es|ing)?\b|\bfell short\b|\bfailed to (?:meet|deliver|hit|achieve)\b", re.I),
    "delivered": re.compile(r"\b(?:delivered|delivers|hit|met|achieved|kept|beat)\b", re.I),
}
_CLAUSE = re.compile(r"[.;:]|,?\s*\b(?:but|while|whereas|although|though|yet)\b|,\s*and\b")
_STOP = {"the", "a", "an", "of", "and", "to", "in", "on", "for", "its", "their", "our", "with", "by", "that", "this", "is",
         "was", "were", "has", "have", "had", "be", "been", "management", "managements", "target", "targets", "goal",
         "goals", "guidance", "promise", "promises", "reliably", "consistently", "largely", "mostly", "it", "they",
         "missed", "miss", "misses", "delivered", "hit", "met", "achieved", "kept", "beat", "fell", "short", "failed"}


def _tokens(s: str) -> set:
    return {t for t in re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", (s or "").lower()) if t not in _STOP}


def credibility_issue(text: str | None, rows: list[dict]) -> str | None:
    """Does the summary call a promise missed/delivered when the final ledger verdict says otherwise?"""
    if not text:
        return None
    for clause in _CLAUSE.split(text):
        for verdict, rx in _OUTCOME_WORDS.items():
            m = rx.search(clause or "")
            if not m or re.search(r"\b(?:not|never|no|without)\s+(?:\w+\s+)?$", clause[:m.start()], re.I):
                continue
            words = _tokens(clause)
            scored = [(len(words & _tokens(r.get("subject"))), r) for r in rows]
            best = max((s for s, _ in scored), default=0)
            about = [r for s, r in scored if s == best and s >= 2]
            if about and not any(r.get("verdict") == verdict for r in about):
                r = about[0]
                return f"Says '{m.group(0)}' about '{r.get('subject')}', which the ledger marks {r.get('verdict')}."
            if not about and not any(r.get("verdict") == verdict for r in rows):
                return f"Says '{m.group(0)}', but no promise in the ledger is {verdict}."
    return None


_SUMMARY = [("delivered", "delivered"), ("missed", "missed"), ("goalposts_moved", "softened or pushed out"),
            ("dropped", "dropped"), ("at_risk", "at risk"), ("on_track", "on track"), ("too_early", "too early to judge")]


def credibility_summary(rows: list[dict]) -> str:
    """The track record stated from the final verdicts — used when the model's summary contradicts them."""
    parts = []
    for verdict, label in _SUMMARY:
        subj = [r["subject"] for r in rows if r.get("verdict") == verdict]
        if subj:
            parts.append(f"{len(subj)} {label} ({'; '.join(subj)})")
    n_unv = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("verdict") == "unverifiable")
    if n_unv:
        parts.append(f"{n_unv} not verifiable from the filings")
    if not parts:
        return ""
    body = parts[0] if len(parts) == 1 else ", ".join(parts[:-1]) + " and " + parts[-1]
    return f"Of {len(rows)} promise{'s' if len(rows) != 1 else ''} tracked: {body}."

```

"""Narrative consistency: the memo's prose must agree with the figures it cites and with the final ledger verdicts.

Regression cases from the production TATATECH memo rebuilt on 2026-11-09 (edc3910), kept in narrative_fixture.json
together with the DIXON and HDFCBANK memos (public data):
  - bull 2 "EBITDA margin improved sequentially to 16.1% in Q2 FY27, validating the promise of sequential margin
    improvement" — the cited pair is Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26 (year-on-year), and the promise (H2 FY27) is too_early;
  - credibility "… but missed the FY27 operating-margin goal" — that row is at_risk.
"""
import copy
import json
import pathlib

import pytest

from finn.pull import ledger, narrative, periods, research, thesis, verify

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent
FIX = json.loads((HERE / "narrative_fixture.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
TT = FIX["TATATECH"]
LATEST = periods.from_calendar(TT["latest_quarter"])  # Q2 FY27
LED = {f"L{i + 1}": r for i, r in enumerate(TT["ledger_rows"])}
BULL2 = TT["thesis"]["bull"][1]


def _fact(fid, value, period, label="EBITDA margin"):
    return {"type": "fact", "id": fid, "label": label, "value": value, "unit": "%", "period": period}


YOY_PAIR = [_fact("X.EBITDA margin.Q2 FY27", 16.1, "Q2 FY27"), _fact("X.EBITDA margin.Q2 FY26", 15.7, "Q2 FY26")]
SEQ_PAIR = [_fact("calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Jun 2026", 16.04, "Jun 2026"), _fact("calc.Q.ebitda_margin.Sep 2026", 16.07, "Sep 2026")]


# ---------- 1. the TATATECH bull point ----------

def test_production_bull_point_is_the_regression_case():
    assert BULL2["point"] == ("EBITDA margin improved sequentially to 16.1% in Q2 FY27, validating the promise of "
                              "sequential margin improvement.")
    assert BULL2["refs"] == ["L3", "X.EBITDA margin.Q2 FY27", "G5.2", "X.EBITDA margin.Q2 FY26"]


def test_year_apart_pair_called_sequential_is_flagged():
    assert narrative.comparison_issue(BULL2["point"], BULL2["evidence"]) == \
        "Calls a Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26 comparison sequential; the same quarter a year apart is year-on-year."


def test_validating_an_unstarted_promise_is_flagged():
    issue = narrative.promise_issue(BULL2["point"], BULL2["refs"], BULL2["evidence"], LED, LATEST)
    assert issue == ("Says a promise is met, but the ledger marks 'H2 FY27 EBITDA margin improvement' too early to judge "
                     "(H2 FY27 hasn't started).")


def test_both_reasons_reach_the_rewrite():
    issues = narrative.thesis_issues(TT["thesis"], {"rows": TT["ledger_rows"]}, LATEST)
    assert list(issues) == ["bull2"]  # the other five TATATECH points pass
    assert "year-on-year" in issues["bull2"]["issue"] and "too early to judge" in issues["bull2"]["issue"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("point,evidence", [
    ("EBITDA margin rose to 16.1% in Q2 FY27 from 15.7% a year earlier.", YOY_PAIR),
    ("EBITDA margin rose year-on-year to 16.1% in Q2 FY27.", YOY_PAIR),
    ("EBITDA margin improved sequentially to 16.07% in Q2 FY27 from 16.04% in Q1 FY27.", SEQ_PAIR),
])
def test_correctly_labelled_comparisons_pass(point, evidence):
    assert narrative.comparison_issue(point, evidence) is None


def test_adjacent_quarters_called_year_on_year_are_flagged():
    assert "sequential" in narrative.comparison_issue("Margin rose 3 bps year-on-year to 16.07%.", SEQ_PAIR)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("point", [
    "EBITDA margin rose to 16.1% in Q2 FY27, consistent with the H2 FY27 margin-improvement guidance, which is untested.",
    "The H2 FY27 margin promise has not yet been validated.",
    "Management has yet to deliver on the H2 FY27 margin target.",
])
def test_untested_promise_described_honestly_passes(point):
    assert narrative.promise_issue(point, BULL2["refs"], BULL2["evidence"], LED, LATEST) is None


def test_validating_a_delivered_promise_passes():
    point = "Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin of 16.03% beat the Q2 run-rate, validating the promise."
    assert narrative.promise_issue(point, ["L3"], [], LED, LATEST) is None  # L3 = Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin, delivered


def test_unstarted_guidance_without_a_ledger_row_is_still_checked():
    g = {"type": "guidance", "id": "G9.9", "call": "Q2 FY27", "horizon": "H2 FY27", "statement": "Margins will improve in H2."}
    assert "H2 FY27, which hasn't started" in narrative.promise_issue("This confirms the margin guidance.", ["G9.9"], [g], {}, LATEST)


# ---------- 2. the credibility summary ----------

def test_production_credibility_contradicting_the_ledger_is_flagged():
    assert "missed the FY27 operating‑margin goal" in TT["credibility"]
    assert narrative.credibility_issue(TT["credibility"], TT["ledger_rows"]) == \
        "Says 'missed' about 'FY27 operating margin run rate', which the ledger marks at_risk."


def test_credibility_guard_replaces_it_with_the_ledger_record():
    result = {"rows": copy.deepcopy(TT["ledger_rows"]), "credibility": TT["credibility"]}
    ledger._credibility_guard(result)
    assert result["credibility"] == (
        "Of 7 promises tracked: 2 delivered (Q4 FY26 sequential revenue growth; Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin), 1 at risk "
        "(FY27 operating margin run rate), 1 on track (FY27 revenue growth), 1 too early to judge (H2 FY27 EBITDA "
        "margin improvement) and 2 not verifiable from the filings.")
    assert result["credibility_check"]["replaced"] == TT["credibility"]
    assert "missed" not in result["credibility"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", [
    "Management reliably hit sequential revenue and margin targets; the FY27 operating-margin goal is at risk.",
    "Management delivered on Q4 FY26 sequential revenue growth and EBITDA margin; FY27 margins are under pressure.",
])
def test_consistent_credibility_is_kept(text):
    result = {"rows": copy.deepcopy(TT["ledger_rows"]), "credibility": text}
    ledger._credibility_guard(result)
    assert result["credibility"] == text and "credibility_check" not in result


@pytest.mark.parametrize("sym", ["DIXON", "HDFCBANK"])
def test_dixon_and_hdfcbank_prose_raises_no_flags(sym):
    m = FIX[sym]
    assert narrative.credibility_issue(m["credibility"], m["ledger_rows"]) is None  # "missing data", "capex … misses"
    assert narrative.thesis_issues(m["thesis"], {"rows": m["ledger_rows"]}, periods.from_calendar(m["latest_quarter"])) == {}


def test_missed_with_no_missed_promise_at_all_is_flagged():
    rows = [{"subject": "FY27 revenue growth", "verdict": "on_track"}]
    assert narrative.credibility_issue("Management missed its guidance.", rows) == \
        "Says 'missed', but no promise in the ledger is missed."


# ---------- the research pipeline acts on the flags ----------

def _secs():
    rows = copy.deepcopy(TT["ledger_rows"])
    for r in rows:
        r.setdefault("facts", []), r.setdefault("delivered", ""), r.setdefault("why", "")
    return {"thesis": copy.deepcopy(TT["thesis"]), "ledger": {"rows": rows}}


def test_flagged_point_is_rewritten_even_when_the_second_model_misses_it(monkeypatch):
    # In production the verifier passed bull 2. FINN's own check must still send it back for a rewrite.
    monkeypatch.setattr(research.verify, "check", lambda claims: {c["id"]: {"supported": True, "issue": ""} for c in claims})
    seen = {}

    def rewrite(fin, calls, led, feedback=None):
        seen["feedback"] = feedback
        th = copy.deepcopy(TT["thesis"])
        th["bull"][1] = {"point": "EBITDA margin rose to 16.1% in Q2 FY27 from 15.7% a year earlier; the H2 FY27 "
                                  "improvement promise is still untested.", "refs": BULL2["refs"], "evidence": BULL2["evidence"]}
        return th

    monkeypatch.setattr(research.thesis, "build", rewrite)
    secs = _secs()
    research._verify({"trajectory": {"quarterly": [{"period": "Sep 2026"}]}}, [], secs)
    assert len(seen["feedback"]) == 1 and seen["feedback"][0].startswith('"EBITDA margin improved sequentially')
    assert secs["verification"]["rewrote_thesis"] is True and secs["verification"]["flagged"] == 0
    assert secs["thesis"]["bull"][1]["verified"] is True


def test_point_still_wrong_after_the_rewrite_stays_flagged(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(research.verify, "check", lambda claims: {c["id"]: {"supported": True, "issue": ""} for c in claims})
    monkeypatch.setattr(research.thesis, "build", lambda fin, calls, led, feedback=None: copy.deepcopy(TT["thesis"]))
    secs = _secs()
    research._verify({"trajectory": {"quarterly": [{"period": "Sep 2026"}]}}, [], secs)
    p = secs["thesis"]["bull"][1]
    assert p["verified"] is False and "year-on-year" in p["issue"] and secs["verification"]["flagged"] == 1


def test_narrative_checks_run_when_no_verifier_model_is_available(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(research.verify, "check", lambda claims: {})
    monkeypatch.setattr(research.thesis, "build", lambda fin, calls, led, feedback=None: copy.deepcopy(TT["thesis"]))
    secs = _secs()
    research._verify({"trajectory": {"quarterly": [{"period": "Sep 2026"}]}}, [], secs)
    assert secs["verification"]["status"] == "narrative_only" and secs["thesis"]["bull"][1]["verified"] is False


# ---------- what the thesis and verifier models are told ----------

def _fin():
    facts = {f["id"]: {k: f[k] for k in ("id", "label", "value", "unit", "period")} for f in YOY_PAIR + SEQ_PAIR}
    facts["calc.Q.revenue_qoq.Sep 2026"] = {"id": "calc.Q.revenue_qoq.Sep 2026", "label": "Revenue growth QoQ (sequential)",
                                            "value": 2.0, "unit": "%", "period": "Sep 2026"}
    return {"signals": [], "facts": facts, "trajectory": {"quarterly": [{"period": "Jun 2026"}, {"period": "Sep 2026"}]}}

                "bear": [], "watch": None}

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-11-09T20:35:45Z

Both inconsistencies are now caught and corrected in code. Everything is local and uncommitted, all 157 backend tests pass, and production is untouched.

## Where they came from
- **Bull point:** the thesis model wrote it. Three gaps let it through:
  - The thesis prompt didn't say what period each guidance item covers or what the ledger decided about it.
  - The only margin pair the model could cite was Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26, which is a year apart. It had no quarter-on-quarter margin figures.
  - The second-model check passed the claim anyway.
- **Credibility summary:** the ledger model writes it in the same call as its verdicts, before FINN's own checks run. Nothing compared it with the final verdicts.

## The fix
I added checks in code that don't depend on a model:

1. **Comparison wording.** A sentence that says "sequentially" must cite figures for adjacent quarters, and one that says "year-on-year" must cite the same quarter a year apart. Otherwise it is flagged.
2. **Promise claims.** A sentence may say a promise was met, validated or delivered only if every promise it cites is `delivered` in the ledger. Negated wording such as "has not yet been validated" is allowed. If the promise's period hasn't started, the flag says so.
3. **Credibility summary.** If it says "missed" or "met" about a promise whose final verdict differs, FINN replaces it with a summary of the actual verdicts.

How the checks are used:
- **They always run,** including when the second model is unavailable.
- **Flagged points get one rewrite.** A point that is still wrong after the rewrite shows a warning in the memo.
- **The prompts are tighter.** The thesis now sees each guidance item's period and ledger verdict, plus the latest exact quarter-on-quarter figures. Both the thesis and verifier prompts state the sequential vs year-on-year rule.

## Files changed
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [narrative.py](backend/finn/pull/narrative.py) (new) | The three checks |
| [ledger.py](backend/finn/pull/ledger.py) | Credibility check after the verdicts are final; prompt rule |
| [thesis.py](backend/finn/pull/thesis.py) | Guidance shows period and ledger verdict; adjacent-quarter margins; prompt rules |
| [verify.py](backend/finn/pull/verify.py) | Verifier rules on comparison periods and promise claims; guidance evidence shows the ledger verdict |
| [research.py](backend/finn/pull/research.py) | Runs FINN's checks with the second model and feeds them into the rewrite. Also fixes a crash that would have hit when only FINN's checks run. |
| [api.ts](frontend/src/lib/api.ts), [Memo.tsx](frontend/src/screens/Memo.tsx) | Warning on a bull or bear point that is still flagged |
| [test_narrative.py](backend/tests/test_narrative.py), [narrative_fixture.json](backend/tests/narrative_fixture.json) (new) | 26 tests; the fixture is from the production TATATECH, DIXON and HDFCBANK memos |

## Tests
- **Backend:** 157 passed, 0 failed (131 existing + 26 new).
- **New tests on the old code:** 9 of 26 fail. Those 9 cover the pipeline changes; the other 17 test the new checks directly.
- **Frontend build:** succeeds.

## Production TATATECH memo
I only read it, with GET requests. It is unchanged since the 20:23:51 rebuild and still shows both problems.
- **Bull point 2** is flagged for both reasons: the comparison is year-on-year, and it says a promise was met that the ledger marks `too_early`.
- **The credibility summary** is flagged because it says "missed" about the FY27 operating-margin goal, which is `at_risk`. FINN's replacement would read:
  > Of 7 promises tracked: 2 delivered (Q4 FY26 sequential revenue growth; Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin), 1 at risk (FY27 operating margin run rate), 1 on track (FY27 revenue growth), 1 too early to judge (H2 FY27 EBITDA margin improvement) and 2 not verifiable from the filings.
- **The other 5 TATATECH points, and all DIXON and HDFCBANK prose, raise no flags.** Two false positives on DIXON and HDFCBANK came up during development and are fixed ("missing data" no longer reads as "missed").

## Remaining issues
1. **The live memo still has both errors** until you approve committing, deploying and one more TATATECH rebuild.
2. **The checks match words, not meaning.** A paraphrase like "bears out the guidance" could get past the promise check. The fallback summary is accurate but drops the model's qualitative read.
3. **A rebuild can still produce a bad point.** If the model writes another one, it gets one rewrite. If it is still wrong, it stays in the memo with a warning rather than being removed.
4. **The changes are uncommitted on local `main`.** When you approve, I'll commit on a branch first, as last time, so nothing deploys before you say so.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-11-10T05:08:44Z

The preview's Brief fails because the preview build has **no backend URL**, not because of anything in PR #1. Without the URL, the app calls `/api/digest` on the preview's own Vercel domain, and Vercel returns its standard "NOT_FOUND" page, which is the exact text you saw. Nothing was changed while investigating.

## What I found
1. **Where the request goes:** the Brief page requests `/api/digest?hours=…`. The API base URL comes from `VITE_API_URL`, which is fixed when the frontend is built ([api.ts:1](frontend/src/lib/api.ts#L1)). If it's missing, the base is an empty string, so the request goes to the preview's own domain. Vercel serves no `/api` routes, so it answers 404. Even the production domain returns the same 404 text if you request `/api/digest` on it directly.
2. **Production versus preview:**
   - **Production** (eosin domain) has `https://finn-api-bbyo.onrender.com` built in, and Render accepts requests from that domain.
   - **The preview** is behind Vercel's login, so I couldn't download its bundle. Its 404 can only happen if the build has no backend URL (or one that points at a Vercel domain). The most likely cause is that `VITE_API_URL` is set in Vercel only for the **Production** environment, not **Preview**.
3. **Why Research looked fine:** its company list is hard-coded (`SUGGESTED` in Research.tsx). The list that does come from the API, "recent memos", just hides itself when its request fails. So Research would have looked normal without any working connection.
4. **PR #1 didn't cause it.** Its only frontend changes are two optional fields on one type and a warning label. `vercel.json`, the Vite config and `package.json` are unchanged, and the API base logic is the same as in production. Any branch preview would show this.
5. **There is a second, hidden blocker.** Render only accepts requests from the production domain. A test request from the preview's domain got `400 Bad Request` with no permission header, while the eosin domain got `200`. So adding the URL alone would just turn the 404 into a "Failed to fetch" error.

**Classification:** this is a preview environment setup issue. It isn't a frontend routing bug, a missing API endpoint, or a regression from the PR.

**To confirm in about 30 seconds:**
- In the preview, open DevTools → Network and reload the Brief page. The failing request should go to `https://…-[REDACTED_VERCEL_PREVIEW]/api/digest`, not to `finn-api-bbyo.onrender.com`.
- In Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables, check whether `VITE_API_URL` is scoped to **Production** only.

## Safest fix
**Recommended: don't connect previews to the production API, and review this PR another way.** In this app, opening a memo screen starts a **production rebuild** if the memo is more than 24 hours old. DIXON and HDFCBANK pass that mark at about 14:47 today, so clicking around the preview could rebuild them. The PR's real changes are in the backend narrative checks, which the 157 local tests cover. Its UI change can be checked in the local dev server against the local SQLite backend. Treat the Brief error in the preview as expected.

**If you want working previews,** each option needs your approval:
- **A. Configuration only, no code:**
  1. In Vercel, add `VITE_API_URL=https://finn-api-bbyo.onrender.com` for **Preview** (it's a public URL, not a secret).
  2. On Render, add the preview domain to `FINN_CORS_ORIGINS`, which changes a production environment variable.
  3. Redeploy the preview.
- **B. Code change:** add a rewrite in `vercel.json` that sends `/api/*` to Render. Previews would then work without any environment variable or Render change.

Both options give previews full access to production, including the rebuild-on-open behaviour. So if you choose one, I'd first make preview builds read-only, for example by not sending memo POSTs from preview builds.

I've stopped here, with no code changes, merges, pushes or deploys.

**Recommendation: needs changes before merging.** There are no critical issues, but two important ones would show up on the very TATATECH rebuild this PR is meant for. I reviewed all 9 files against `edc3910` and changed nothing. I didn't re-run the tests, since the branch hasn't changed since the last run (157 passed). The checks below were run on local functions and saved snapshots only.

## Critical issues
None. There are no crashes, data writes, schema or API changes, and the code paths are only used when a memo is built.

## Important issues
1. **The comparison check flags correct sentences** ([narrative.py:46](backend/finn/pull/narrative.py#L46)).
   - It fires on any use of "sequential" when only year-apart figures are cited, even when the word names the *promise*.
   - Both of these got flagged in my probes:
     - "…rose to 16.1% from 15.7% a year earlier; the H2 FY27 sequential improvement promise is still untested."
     - "…rose year-on-year to 16.1%, consistent with guidance for sequential margin improvement…"
   - A rewrite of TATATECH bull 2 will very likely name that promise, so a correct point would be marked "⚠ disputed".
   - Fix: ignore "sequential" when it's part of a promise or guidance phrase, or only check the clause that describes the cited figures. Add these two sentences as passing tests.
2. **After the rewrite, points the verifier never checked are recorded as verified** ([research.py:94](backend/finn/pull/research.py#L94)).
   - The second `judge` call's "did the verifier run?" result is thrown away.
   - If the verifier is unavailable (quota) or skips some points when the rewrite is checked:
     - those points default to `verified: True`;
     - `verification.status` still says `"done"`.
   - The old code had a related problem (it kept stale results from the first draft). This PR swaps it for a different silent failure.
   - Fix: record whether the second pass ran. Leave unchecked points as `verified: null`, and set status to something like `"rewrite_unverified"`.
3. **The deploy has a visible effect on an existing memo, with no rebuild.** The stored HDFCBANK memo already has 3 points with `verified: false`:
   - bull 2 ("not NIM");
   - bear 1 ("No FY24 ROAA figure");
   - bear 2 ("lacks NIM reference").

   The new frontend will show "⚠ disputed by FINN's check" on those 3 straight away. That's arguably correct, but it should be your decision. DIXON and TATATECH have none.
4. **Extra model usage.** A FINN-only flag now triggers the thesis rewrite plus another verifier call. That adds 2 model calls per affected build against the Gemini free tier (about 20 requests per day per model).

## Minor issues
- **Credibility check:**
  - It only checks "missed" and "delivered" wording; "on track" or "at risk" claims aren't checked.
  - It reads "didn't miss" as "missed", because it doesn't treat "n't" as a negation, so a correct summary gets replaced.
  - The replacement summary has no length limit.
  - When the summary is replaced, `credibility_check` is saved but never shown in the app.
- **Ledger verdict for shared guidance** ([thesis.py:56](backend/finn/pull/thesis.py#L56)): if one guidance item feeds two ledger rows with different verdicts, the prompt shows whichever row comes last.
- **The promise check is broad.** "beat" or "confirms … guidance" counts as claiming success against *any* promise the point cites. That's strict, but it can trigger rewrites for loose wording.
- **The warning's reason is hidden on phones** ([Memo.tsx:119](frontend/src/screens/Memo.tsx#L119)). It's in a hover-only `title`, which doesn't work on touch screens, and this is a mobile-first app. Also, "disputed by FINN's check" appears for the second model's flags too, not just FINN's own checks.
- **The watch point isn't checked** by either the verifier or FINN's checks. This was already the case before the PR.

## Your review questions
- **Wiring:** correct. FINN's checks use the final ledger, run even without the verifier, and the verifier's own objection takes priority.
- **One-time rewrite:** it can't silently drop a flag that FINN's own checks still find. It can wrongly mark a point verified (issue 2), and it can mislabel a correct point because of issue 1. It rewrites all 6 points, which are then judged again.
- **Credibility:** correct for the TATATECH case and causes no false flags on DIXON or HDFCBANK. The limitations are listed above.
- **Frontend:** ungrounded points show only "unverified". Flagged points show "disputed". Verified points and older memos without the field show nothing. That's correct.
- **Test coverage:**
  - Covered: the exact TATATECH regressions, rewrite and flag handling, prompt contents, and a no-false-flag check on all stored DIXON and HDFCBANK prose.
  - Missing: issue 1's sentences, a second-pass verifier outage, the "n't" negation, and a full `ledger.build` run that tests the credibility check.
- **Production side effects:** none on stored data. Merging and deploying changes only future builds, plus the HDFCBANK warnings and the extra model calls above.

Fixing issues 1 and 2 with tests is a small change. After that, it's safe to merge, as long as you're happy for the HDFCBANK warnings to appear.

from . import periods

# ---------- comparison wording ----------

_SEQUENTIAL = re.compile(r"\bsequential(?:ly)?\b|\bquarter[- ]on[- ]quarter\b|\bq-?o-?q\b|\bfrom the (?:previous|prior|preceding) quarter\b", re.I)
_YEAR_ON_YEAR = re.compile(r"\byear[- ]on[- ]year\b|\by-?o-?y\b|\bfrom a year (?:earlier|ago)\b", re.I)


def _quarterly_pairs(evidence: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[tuple], list[tuple]]:
    """(adjacent pairs, year-apart pairs) among the cited quarterly figures, per metric."""
    by_metric: dict[str, set] = {}
    for e in evidence:
        fid = str(e.get("id") or "")
        if e.get("type") != "fact" or "value" not in e or "." not in fid:
            continue
        p = periods.fact_period(fid, e.get("period"))
        if p and p.kind == "quarter":
            by_metric.setdefault(fid.rsplit(".", 1)[0], set()).add(p.start)
    adjacent, year_apart = [], []
    for metric, qs in by_metric.items():
        for a in qs:
            for b in qs:
                if b == a.shift(1):
                    adjacent.append((metric, a, b))
                if b == a.shift(4):
                    year_apart.append((metric, a, b))
    return adjacent, year_apart


def comparison_issue(point: str, evidence: list[dict]) -> str | None:
    adjacent, year_apart = _quarterly_pairs(evidence)
    if _SEQUENTIAL.search(point) and year_apart and not adjacent:
        _, a, b = year_apart[0]
        return f"Calls a {b.label} vs {a.label} comparison sequential; the same quarter a year apart is year-on-year."
    if _YEAR_ON_YEAR.search(point) and adjacent and not year_apart:
        _, a, b = adjacent[0]
        return f"Calls a {b.label} vs {a.label} comparison year-on-year; adjacent quarters are sequential."
    return None
```

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-11-10T05:16:02Z

Both fixes are committed as **`64b8a13`** on `fix/narrative-consistency` and pushed. All 169 backend tests pass, and the frontend build succeeds.

## Changed files
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [narrative.py](backend/finn/pull/narrative.py) | **Fix 1.** A "sequential" or "year-on-year" mention is treated as a claim about the cited figures only if it doesn't name a promise in its own clause. |
| [research.py](backend/finn/pull/research.py) | **Fix 2.** The second verifier pass is now recorded. Points the verifier didn't judge get `verified: null` instead of being marked verified. |
| [test_narrative.py](backend/tests/test_narrative.py) | 12 new tests, and 2 existing ones extended. |
| [api.ts](frontend/src/lib/api.ts) | One-line type change: `verified` may be `null`. The memo screen only warns on `false`, so unchecked points show no badge. |

**Fix 1:** both sentences from the review now pass. Sentences that really do describe year-apart figures as sequential are still flagged, including the original "improved sequentially to 16.1%".

**Fix 2:** a point is `verified: true` only if the verifier judged its current text supported. The verification record now shows:
- `recheck`: `done`, `unavailable`, or empty when there was no rewrite;
- `unchecked`: how many points the verifier didn't judge;
- `status`: `rewrite_unverified` when the second pass was unavailable.

## Tests
- **Backend:** 169 passed, 0 failed (157 before, plus 12 new).
  - Fix 1: the two review sentences, still-flagged variants, and the matching year-on-year case.

- **The new tests catch the old code:** against `552cd5a`, 10 of them fail.

  - DIXON and HDFCBANK: no flags.

- **Frontend build:** succeeds.

- **Branch:** `fix/narrative-consistency` at `64b8a13`, the same locally and on GitHub. The working tree is clean.
- **`main`:** still `edc3910` on GitHub. Nothing was merged or pushed to `main`, and nothing was deployed.
- **Production:** not touched. No production requests, no rebuild, and no Vercel or Render setting changed.

Vercel will probably build a new preview of PR #1 for this commit. It will show the same Brief 404 as before, since the preview configuration is unchanged.

from ..config import UA
from ..db import PriceEOD, session


def _upsert(rows: list[dict]):
    with session() as s:
        for r in rows:
            s.merge(PriceEOD(**r))


def history_many(symbols, days: int = 90) -> dict[str, list[PriceEOD]]:
    """history() for many symbols in ONE query — a remote database makes per-symbol queries expensive.

    Same semantics as history(): the last `days` rows per symbol whatever their dates (so stale data still renders),
    via ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY symbol ORDER BY date DESC). Works on SQLite and Postgres.
    """
    symbols = sorted(set(symbols))
    if not symbols:
        return {}
    rn = func.row_number().over(partition_by=PriceEOD.symbol, order_by=PriceEOD.date.desc()).label("rn")
    ranked = select(PriceEOD, rn).where(PriceEOD.symbol.in_(symbols)).subquery()
    latest = aliased(PriceEOD, ranked)
    out: dict[str, list[PriceEOD]] = {s: [] for s in symbols}
    with session() as s:
        for r in s.scalars(select(latest).where(ranked.c.rn <= days).order_by(latest.symbol, latest.date)):
            out[r.symbol].append(r)
    return out


def history(symbol: str, days: int = 90) -> list[PriceEOD]:
    with session() as s:
        rows = s.scalars(select(PriceEOD).where(PriceEOD.symbol == symbol).order_by(PriceEOD.date.desc()).limit(days))
        return list(reversed(list(rows)))
```

The local TATATECH rebuild on the merged code is correct on every check except one. FINN's own comparison check wrongly marked a correct bear point as disputed. Production and the local DIXON and HDFCBANK memos are untouched.

## Isolation
- **Code:** the checked-out tree is identical to `016a6d6`.
- **Database:** the build process ran on SQLite (`backend/finn.db`).
  - `config.py` only loads `backend/.env`, where `DATABASE_URL` is blank, and the shell doesn't set it.
  - The local database lacks two memos that exist only in production, so it is separate from Neon.
- **No production writes:** the only production request was one read-only GET of the memo list afterwards.
- **No TATATECH memo existed locally,** so there was nothing to back up. I backed up the whole local database instead, at `~\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\3d6517633a89a6f0\c363bd54-6dbf-4695-9f84-97a9ce39aca0\scratchpad\local\finn.db.before-tatatech`. I compared against the last production version (built on `edc3910`), using a copy saved earlier.

## The build
Exactly one build ran: status `done`, no errors, 76 seconds, 15 model calls. Groq and Gemini rate limits made the router fall back to other models. Local builds use the same API keys as production, so this used shared quota.

## Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| **Fiscal periods** | Audit: 6 period-specific rows, **0 failing** (exit code 0) |
| **Exact margins** | Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin is `delivered` on `calc.Q.ebitda_margin` (16.03% vs 15.72%), with no rounded OPM % used |
| **Ledger verdicts** | Q4 FY26 revenue growth `delivered` (+15.1%). H2 FY27 margin `too_early`. FY27 operating margin `at_risk`. FY27 revenue `on_track`. |
| **Quotes and references** | All 14 quotes word-for-word on the cited page. `validate_memo.py`: **all hard checks passed** |
| **Credibility summary** | Consistent with the verdicts. It calls the FY27 margin goal "at risk", not "missed", so no replacement was needed. |
| **Sequential vs year-on-year** | bull 3 correctly says "year-on-year" (Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26). **bear 3 was wrongly flagged** (below) |
| **Second verifier pass** | `status: done`, `recheck: done`, `unchecked: 0`. Fix 2 works: the rewrite was checked and nothing was left unchecked. |
| **Tests** | 169 passed |

## The false positive
Bear 3 reads: "Sequential PAT dropped 5.5% in Sep 2026 (Q2 FY27) versus Jun 2026 (Q1 FY27), with PAT margin declining year-on-year to 10.1%…" The sentence is correct, and the second model passed it.

FINN's comparison check flagged it anyway, because it only recognises *pairs* of quarterly figures. The sequential claim rests on `calc.Q.pat_qoq.Sep 2026`, a single figure that is already a quarter-on-quarter change. The only pair cited is the year-apart PAT margins.

The draft it replaced was also correct, so the check caused an unnecessary rewrite and a wrong "⚠ disputed" label. The likely fix is to treat quarter-on-quarter growth figures as sequential evidence and year-on-year growth figures as year-on-year evidence. I haven't changed any code.

+ def _figure_clauses(rx: re.Pattern, point: str) -> list[str]:
+     """Clauses in which a mention of this comparison type describes the figures (not a promise)."""
+     out = []
+     for clause in _CLAUSE_BREAK.split(point):
+         for m in rx.finditer(clause or ""):
+             if not (_PROMISE_BEFORE.search(clause[:m.start()]) or _PROMISE_AFTER.match(clause[m.end():])):
+                 out.append(clause)
+                 break
+     return out
+
+
+ def _mislabelled(rx: re.Pattern, point: str, ev: _Evidence, wrong: dict, right: dict) -> str | None:
+     """A clause using this comparison word about a metric whose cited evidence is only the other kind of comparison.
+     The metric is the one the clause names; if it names none of the cited metrics, the whole point's evidence decides."""
+     for clause in _figure_clauses(rx, point):
+         metrics = _named_metrics(clause, ev.metrics) or (ev.metrics if not right else set())
+         for metric in sorted(metrics):
+             if metric in wrong and metric not in right:
+                 return wrong[metric]
+     return None
+
+
+ def comparison_issue(point: str, evidence: list[dict]) -> str | None:
+     ev = _Evidence(evidence)
+     if what := _mislabelled(_SEQUENTIAL, point, ev, ev.yoy, ev.seq):
+         return f"Calls {what} sequential; the same quarter a year apart is year-on-year."
+     if what := _mislabelled(_YEAR_ON_YEAR, point, ev, ev.seq, ev.yoy):
+         return f"Calls {what} year-on-year; adjacent quarters are sequential."
+     return None

+     """The row's title must name the period the promise is about. A model-written subject such as "Q2 FY27 sequential
+     EBITDA margin improvement" for a promise about H2 FY27 is retitled "H2 FY27 …"; a subject that names the promise
+     period (alongside a comparison period, e.g. "Q4 FY26 margin vs Q2 FY26") or no period at all is left alone.

+         return
+     m = named[0][0]
+     r["subject_corrected_from"] = subject
+     r["subject"] = subject[:m.start()] + promise.label + subject[m.end():]

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-11-10T05:49:54Z

Both TATATECH findings are fixed locally, and all 208 backend tests pass. Nothing is committed, and nothing in production was requested, rebuilt or changed. The work is on a new local-only branch, `fix/tatatech-margin-qa`, made from the latest `main` (`5332283`) and not pushed.

## Files changed
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [ledger.py](backend/finn/pull/ledger.py) | **Margin fix.** `_margin_guard` now attaches a named base quarter's exact margin. A new `_base_quarter` reads the base from the guided target first, then the row's subject and promise, then management's statement. **Title fix:** a new `_subject_guard`, run at the end of each row's checks in `build`. |
| [test_margins.py](backend/tests/test_margins.py) | 11 new tests. One existing test now uses a promise with no base quarter, because it asserted the old, incomplete behaviour. |
| [test_periods.py](backend/tests/test_periods.py) | 9 new tests (counting each parametrised case) for the title check. |

No frontend file changed, so I didn't run the frontend build.

## Fix 1: the comparison quarter's margin
- **How it works:** when a single-quarter margin promise names its comparison quarter but only the promised quarter is cited, FINN looks up that quarter's exact margin from the same source and attaches it. It records `attached_fact_ids`, then decides the comparison in code.
- **How the base is read:**
  - "exceed our Q2 run-rate" means the latest Q2 before the promised quarter, so Q2 FY26 here.
  - An explicit "Q2 FY26" is used as written.
  - "Sequential" means the previous quarter.
  - A bare mention of the promised quarter itself, like "For Q4", is ignored.
- **When it can't be done, the row becomes `unverifiable`:**
  - The base has no exact figure (`base_missing`). FINN never estimates it or uses rounded OPM %.
  - The text names two different base quarters (`base_ambiguous`).
  - The only exact base figure comes from a different source than the target's. Sources are never mixed.

## Fix 2: the row title
- If a title names a fiscal period that doesn't overlap the promise's actual period, that label is replaced with the promise period. The original is kept in `subject_corrected_from`, and the verdict isn't touched.
- So "Q2 FY27 sequential EBITDA margin improvement" becomes "**H2 FY27** sequential EBITDA margin improvement", still `too_early`.
- These titles are left alone: the right period, the promise period plus a comparison period, no period at all, or a quarter inside the promised half.

## Tests
- **Backend:** 208 passed, 0 failed (188 before, plus 20 new).
- **The new tests catch the old code:** against the `5332283` version of `ledger.py`, 19 of them fail.
- **Production rows:** both exact rows are covered, including a full `ledger.build` run.
- **The unavailable-base case:** the base becomes `unverifiable` with the reason given, and rounded 16% is never used. The test also covers a model that cited a rounded figure, and a base that exists only in a different source.
- **Other cases:** an explicit base label, a "sequential" base, two bases (ambiguous), a bare "For Q4", and a wrong model verdict being corrected.
- **DIXON, HDFCBANK and TATATECH fixtures:** no title changes.

## Local memo and production replay
I didn't rebuild anything. Replaying the saved rows offline was enough.
- **Local TATATECH memo (05:28:51):** none of its 6 rows changes under the new checks. `validate_memo.py` passes, with all 14 quotes correct.
- **Production rows from the 05:41 rebuild, replayed with the exact margins stored locally:**
  - **Margin row:** now cites 16.03% **and** 15.72%. The comparison is confirmed in code (`above`), and the verdict stays `delivered`. The validator's "15.72 not in cited evidence" warning is gone.
  - **H2 row:** retitled to "H2 FY27 sequential EBITDA margin improvement" and still `too_early`. FINN's credibility summary now uses the correct title.
  - **Audit:** 0 failing.
- **Local DIXON and HDFCBANK:** byte-identical to their backups.

## Remaining limitations
1. **Only explicitly named bases are attached** ("Q2", "Q2 FY26", "sequential"). Phrases like "last year's level", "H1 average" or "previous peak" aren't detected. Those rows behave as before: the model's verdict stands and nothing is attached.
2. **A bare "Qn" always means the most recent earlier Qn.** A promise about a later period phrased that way would be read wrongly. That's rare in practice.
3. **The title check only fixes explicit labels such as "Q2 FY27".** It replaces only the first wrong label and doesn't check the row's promise text, which was already correct here.
4. **Production still shows both problems.** It will until you commit, merge and deploy this branch, and then approve one more TATATECH rebuild.
5. **The changes are uncommitted** on local branch `fix/tatatech-margin-qa`, as you asked.

### 🤖 Claude · 2026-11-10T05:51:54Z

**There is one blocking issue: don't commit yet.** I changed no files, and the probes above were local, read-only function calls.

## Blocking

**1. A quarter mentioned in passing in management's statement is treated as the comparison base. This can flip a correct verdict and disable the range check** ([ledger.py `_base_quarter`, `_margin_guard`](backend/finn/pull/ledger.py)).
- `_base_quarter` falls back to any quarter mentioned in the guidance *statement*, and applies even when the promise has a numeric level target.
- **Probe B1:** the promise is "EBITDA margin above 18% in Q4", and the statement says "Q3 was soft at 14%; for Q4 we expect…". The actual margin was 16.03%, and the model correctly said `missed`.
  - Q3 FY26 was attached as the base.
  - The code compared 16.03% with Q3's 14.13% and changed the verdict to **delivered**.
  - `_range_check` then skipped, because two % figures were now cited.
- **Probe B2:** the same promise without the Q3 mention stays `missed` (range check: below).
- **Probe B3:** a bare *future* quarter is read backwards. "Recover fully by Q4", on a Q2 FY27 promise, became the base **Q4 FY26**.
- **Suggested fix:**
  - Only use a quarter reference that comes with a comparison word, such as "Q2 run-rate", "Q2 level", "than / vs / over Q2", or "sequential".
  - Skip base detection entirely when the guidance has a numeric `low`/`high` target, so the range check decides.
  - Add tests for B1 to B3.

## Medium

**2. The title check renames rows whose title deliberately names the original period** (`_subject_guard`).
- It only compares the title with the *latest* guidance period.
- **Probe H1:** a `goalposts_moved` row titled "FY26 capex target", whose later guidance moved to FY27, was renamed "**FY27** capex target". The title naming the original period is exactly what explains that verdict.
- **Fix:** accept the title if its period overlaps *any* guidance item in the row, or skip `goalposts_moved` and `dropped` rows.

## Low

3. **Year-range labels get mangled.** "FY26-27 capex" becomes "FY27-27 capex" (probe H2), because `_PERIOD_LABEL` only matches the "FY26" part. Either match the full range or skip titles that contain one.
4. **The ambiguous-base path returns before the rounded-to-exact swap.** A row that cited rounded OPM % keeps that rounded figure as its displayed fact. The verdict is still correctly `unverifiable`.
5. **Test gaps:** findings 1 to 3 aren't covered. The fixture tests for DIXON and HDFCBANK only include the facts each row cites, so they can't trigger the base-attachment path.
6. **`subject_corrected_from` and `attached_fact_ids` are saved but never shown** in the app, so a reader can't see that FINN retitled a row or added evidence.

## The five things you asked me to check
- **1. Base-period selection:** incorrect in cases B1 to B3 (finding 1). The named-base cases work: "our Q2 run-rate", an explicit "Q2 FY26", "sequential", and a bare "For Q4".
- **2. Mixing source families:** none found. A base is attached only from the one source that covers both quarters, and if no single source does, the row becomes `unverifiable`.
- **3. Changing legitimate titles or verdicts:**
  - Verdicts: yes, through finding 1.
  - Titles: yes, through findings 2 and 3.
  - The production H2 row and all fixture titles behave correctly.
- **4. DIXON, HDFCBANK and other companies:**
  - HDFCBANK is a bank and has no EBITDA-margin facts, so the margin check doesn't touch it, and its titles contain no periods.
  - DIXON's stored rows don't change.
  - The real risk is future rebuilds for any company with quarter-level margin targets (finding 1) or targets that moved between years (finding 2), DIXON included.
- **5. Out-of-scope changes:** none. Only the three files changed. In `ledger.py`, the only change outside the margin logic is the `_subject_guard` call added to `build`. Moving `_promise()` earlier changes nothing. The one edited existing test was rewritten for a justified reason.

**Verdict:** fix findings 1 and 2, with tests, before committing. Findings 3 to 6 can go in the same change or later.

+ # A fiscal label in a title, matched whole — including year ranges ("FY26-27", "FY2026–27"), which mean the later year.
+ _FY_LABEL = r"FY\s?'?\d{2,4}(?:\s?[-–/]\s?'?\d{2,4})?"
+ _PERIOD_LABEL = re.compile(rf"\b(?:(?:Q[1-4]|H[12])\s?)?{_FY_LABEL}\b", re.I)
+
+
+ def _overlap(a: periods.Period, b: periods.Period) -> bool:
+     return a.start <= b.end and b.start <= a.end
+
+
+ def _subject_guard(r: dict, guidance: dict) -> None:
+     """The row's title must name a period the promise is about. A model-written subject such as "Q2 FY27 sequential
+     EBITDA margin improvement" for a promise only ever about H2 FY27 is retitled "H2 FY27 …".
+
+     Left alone: a title with no fiscal label; one whose period overlaps ANY guidance item in the row (an original
+     period the promise was first made for, or a comparison period alongside it); and every goalposts_moved / dropped
+     row, whose title naming the original period is the point. Only the label changes — never the verdict."""
+     if r.get("verdict") in ("goalposts_moved", "dropped"):
+         return
+     promise = _promise(r, guidance)
+     subject = r.get("subject") or ""
+     named = [(m, periods.resolve(m.group(0), None)) for m in _PERIOD_LABEL.finditer(subject)]
+     named = [(m, p) for m, p in named if p]
+     if not promise or not named:
+         return
+     said = [p for g in r["guidance_ids"] if g in guidance and (p := periods.promise_period(guidance[g]))] or [promise]
+     if any(_overlap(p, g) for _, p in named for g in said):
+         return
+     m = named[0][0]

Not caused by this branch. The DIXON change comes from the rounded-to-exact swap that's been on `main` since `edc3910`:
- The stored DIXON memo was built before that commit, so it still cites screener's rounded `Q.OPM %.Sep 2026`.
- `main` (`5332283`) and this branch make the identical change: the figure becomes the exchange filing's `X.EBITDA margin.Q2 FY27`.
- The verdict stays `at_risk`. Nothing is attached, and the title isn't touched.

All five review findings are fixed. The full backend suite passes with **225 passed, 0 failed**, and nothing was committed. The frontend wasn't touched, so I didn't rebuild it. No production request was sent and no memo was rebuilt.

## Changes, all uncommitted on `fix/tatatech-margin-qa`
| File | What changed in this round |
|---|---|
| [ledger.py](backend/finn/pull/ledger.py) | **Base quarter:** a quarter counts as a base only with a comparison word attached ("Q2 run-rate / level / baseline / exit", "versus / vs / than / above / exceed / beat / over / ahead of / below / compared with / relative to Q2"), and it must be earlier than the promised quarter. The statement counts only for such explicit comparisons. Detection is skipped entirely when the guidance has a numeric `low` or `high`, so the range check decides. **Ambiguous base:** two small helpers, `_margin_families` and `_cite_instead`, now show the promised quarter's exact margin. **Title check:** never renames `goalposts_moved` or `dropped` rows, accepts a title that overlaps any guidance period in the row, and matches fiscal-year ranges like "FY26-27" whole. |
| [test_margins.py](backend/tests/test_margins.py) | 12 more tests, 23 new in total on this branch |
| [test_periods.py](backend/tests/test_periods.py) | 8 more tests, 17 new in total on this branch |

## Tests
- **Backend:** 225 passed, 0 failed (208 before this round; 188 on `main`).
- **The new tests catch the pre-review code:** 13 of them fail against it.
- **Review probes, re-run:**
  - B1 stays `missed`, and the range check runs (16.03% below 18%).
  - B3 finds no base.
  - H1 keeps its "FY26 capex target" title.
  - H2 leaves "FY26-27 capex" unchanged.
- **Covered by new tests:**
  - B1, B2 and B3.
  - Statement wording that is an explicit comparison (used) vs a passing mention or a deadline (ignored).
  - A later quarter named in a comparison, which is ignored.
  - An ambiguous base showing the exact Q4 figure, and showing nothing invented when no exact figure exists.
  - Moved and dropped titles, original-period titles, a period that matches no guidance, and FY ranges (unchanged, or replaced whole).

## The original TATATECH defects stay fixed
I replayed the saved production rows from the 05:41 rebuild offline:
- **Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin:** cites 16.03% and 15.72% (`above`), still `delivered`. The validator's "15.72 not in cited evidence" warning is gone.
- **H2 row:** retitled "H2 FY27 sequential EBITDA margin improvement", still `too_early`.
- **The other 5 rows:** unchanged.
- **Audit:** 0 failing.
- **Local TATATECH memo:** none of its rows changes, and `validate_memo.py` passes with all 14 quotes correct.

## DIXON and HDFCBANK
- **Fixtures:** all titles, verdicts and cited facts unchanged.
- **Stored local memos:** byte-identical to their backups.
- **Under the new code:**
  - HDFCBANK: no change.
  - DIXON: one row would change its displayed fact (the swap described above). The verdict stays the same, and the change comes from `main`, not this branch.

## Remaining limitations
1. **Base detection only knows certain words.** It recognises the comparison words listed above. Other phrasings, like "best-ever quarter", "last year's level" or "H1 average", aren't detected, so the model's verdict stands with no base attached.
2. **Numeric targets switch off base detection for the whole row.** A row mixing a level target with a quarter comparison ("above 18% and ahead of Q2") is judged only by the range check.
3. **A bare "Qn" in a comparison means the most recent earlier Qn.** An explicit later quarter is ignored.
4. **The title check fixes only explicit fiscal labels,** replaces the first one, and doesn't touch the promise text.
5. **New fields aren't shown in the app:** `attached_fact_ids`, `subject_corrected_from` and `margin_check` are saved but not displayed.
6. **Production still shows the original two problems.** That lasts until this branch is committed, merged and deployed, and one more TATATECH rebuild is approved.

+ _CLAUSE_SEP = re.compile(r",\s+|;\s+|\s+[—–]\s+|\s+-\s+")
+
+
+ def trim_unmet_promise_claim(point: str, refs: list[str], evidence: list[dict], ledger_rows: dict[str, dict],
+                              latest: periods.FQ | None) -> tuple[str, list[str], list[dict]] | None:
+     """Last resort for a point that, after its rewrite, still says an untested or unmet promise was met: drop the clause
+     that says so ("…, validating sequential margin improvement guidance") when the rest of the sentence stands on its
+     own as a figure-based claim, and drop the references only that clause used (the promise's guidance / ledger row).
+
+     Returns (point, refs, evidence) — which must pass every narrative check — or None when the claim is the main
+     clause and there is nothing sound to keep. The caller re-verifies the trimmed text.
+     """
+     if not promise_issue(point, refs, evidence, ledger_rows, latest):
+         return None
+     m = next((m for m in _CLAIMS_ACHIEVED.finditer(point)
+               if not _NEGATED.search(point[:m.start()]) and not _NEGATION_INSIDE.search(m.group(0))), None)
+     before = [s for s in _CLAUSE_SEP.finditer(point) if s.end() <= m.start()] if m else []
+     if not before:
+         return None
+     after = next((s for s in _CLAUSE_SEP.finditer(point) if s.start() >= m.end()), None)
+     kept = (point[:before[-1].start()] + (point[after.start():] if after else "")).strip().rstrip(".,;") + "."
+     if not re.search(r"\d", kept):
+         return None
+     unmet = [r for r in _cited_promises(refs, ledger_rows) if r.get("verdict") != "delivered"]
+     unmet_ids = {g for r in unmet for g in r.get("guidance_ids") or []}
+     drop = {ref for ref in refs if (ref in ledger_rows and ledger_rows[ref] in unmet) or ref in unmet_ids}
+     drop |= {e.get("id") for e in evidence if e.get("type") == "guidance" and latest
+              and (p := periods.promise_period(e)) and p.start > latest}
+     if len(refs) == len(evidence) and any(r not in drop for r in refs):
+         pairs = [(r, e) for r, e in zip(refs, evidence) if r not in drop]
+         refs, evidence = [r for r, _ in pairs], [e for _, e in pairs]
+     if comparison_issue(kept, evidence) or promise_issue(kept, refs, evidence, ledger_rows, latest):
+         return None
+     return kept, refs, evidence
+

+ FRESH_FOR = dt.timedelta(hours=24)            # a done / partial memo younger than this is not rebuilt on view
+ RUNNING_TTL = dt.timedelta(minutes=10)        # a stored "running" state younger than this: a build is in progress
+ RETRY_AFTER_FAILURE = dt.timedelta(minutes=30)  # after a failed build, wait this long before an automatic retry
+
+
+ def _age(ts: str | None) -> dt.timedelta | None:
+     return now() - dt.datetime.fromisoformat(ts) if ts else None
+
+
+ def _complete(memo: dict | None) -> bool:
+     """A finished memo worth keeping: done, with its Promise Ledger."""
+     return bool(memo and memo.get("status") == "done" and (memo.get("sections") or {}).get("ledger"))
+
+
+ def _hold(prev: dict | None, force: bool) -> str | None:
+     """Why a build must NOT start now, or None. A build already in progress — in this process or, via its stored
+     "running" state, in another (deploy overlap, restart) — blocks even an explicit rebuild; freshness and the
+     post-failure cooldown only hold back automatic (on-view) rebuilds."""
+     if not prev:
+         return None
+     if prev.get("status") == "running" and (a := _age(prev.get("started") or prev.get("updated"))) is not None \
+             and a < RUNNING_TTL:
+         return "in_progress"
+     if force:
+         return None
+     if prev.get("status") in ("done", "partial") and not prev.get("refresh_failed") and _age(prev.get("updated")) < FRESH_FOR:
+         return "fresh"
+     failed_at = (prev.get("refresh_failed") or {}).get("at") or (prev.get("updated") if prev.get("status") == "error" else None)
+     if failed_at and _age(failed_at) < RETRY_AFTER_FAILURE:
+         return "cooling_down"
+     return None
+
+
+ def build(sym: str, force: bool = False, previous: dict | None = None) -> dict:
+     """Build a memo. If the build does not finish ("partial" / "error") and the company already had a complete memo,
+     that memo is kept — marked with refresh_failed — rather than replaced by a broken one. `previous` is the memo as
+     it was before start() stored its "running" placeholder."""
+     sym = sym.upper().strip()
+     prev = previous if previous is not None else get(sym)
+     if prev and not force and prev.get("status") in ("done", "partial") and _age(prev.get("updated")) < FRESH_FOR:
+         return prev
+     state = _build(sym)
+     if state.get("status") != "done" and _complete(prev):
+         kept = {**prev, "refresh_failed": {"at": now().isoformat(), "status": state.get("status"),
+                                            "errors": state.get("errors") or []}}
+         kv_set(_key(sym), kept)
+         return kept
+     return state
+
