"""Transcript guidance extraction: verbatim-quote matching across page breaks, and wrong-shaped model output.

HDFCBANK's transcripts repeat a running header on every page ("HDFC Bank Limited / July 18, 2026 / Page 3 of 16 /
Classification - Internal"). find_quote joins a page with the next so a quote may span the break, but the header sat
between the two halves, so a verbatim quote crossing any of the 31 mid-sentence breaks in the five calls could never
match. Its Q4 FY26 call was lost entirely to "'str' object has no attribute 'get'" from a wrong-shaped model answer.
No database, network or model: docs.pages and chat_json are replaced.
"""
import pytest

from finn.pull import transcripts
from finn.sources import docs

HEADER = "HDFC Bank Limited \nJuly 18, 2026 \nPage {n} of 16 \nClassification - Internal"


def _doc(*bodies):
    pages = [HEADER.format(n=i + 1) + "\n" + b for i, b in enumerate(bodies)]
    return {"url": "u", "sha": "s", "n": len(pages), "pages": pages}


DOC = _doc(
    "Sashidhar Jagdishan:\nWe have spent a large part of the month of June in completing the documentation",
    "and approvals necessary from our side. We expect deposit growth to stay ahead of loans over the next year.",
    "Moderator:\nThe next question is from the line of Mr. Rahul Jain from Goldman Sachs.\nRahul Jain:\n"
    "Will margins expand next year?\nSrinivasan Vaidyanathan:\nMargins should improve as deposits reprice",
    "Moderator:\nThank you. We will now take the next question and the trajectory will be upward",
)


# ---------- page breaks ----------

def test_a_verbatim_quote_across_a_page_break_matches_without_the_running_header():
    quote = "completing the documentation and approvals necessary from our side"
    assert docs.find_quote(DOC, quote) == 1


def test_the_header_lines_are_found_from_the_document_and_speaker_labels_are_not_header():
    furniture = docs._furniture(DOC["pages"])
    assert {"HDFC Bank Limited", "July 18, 2026", "Classification - Internal"} <= furniture
    assert "Moderator:" not in furniture


def test_only_the_lines_at_the_break_are_dropped():
    w = docs.window(DOC, 0)
    assert w.startswith("HDFC Bank Limited")                       # page 1's own header is untouched
    assert "the documentation\nand approvals" in w                    # page 2's header is gone at the join
    assert docs.window(DOC, 3) == DOC["pages"][3]                     # the last page has nothing to join


@pytest.mark.parametrize("quote", [
    "completing the paperwork and approvals necessary from our side",   # a word changed
    "the documentation HDFC Bank Limited and approvals",                # not what was said
    "Margins should improve as deposits reprice the trajectory will be upward",   # skips the next speaker's label
])
def test_quotes_that_are_not_verbatim_still_fail(quote):
    assert docs.find_quote(DOC, quote) is None


def test_a_bare_number_at_a_page_edge_is_text_not_a_page_number():
    doc = _doc("Deposits grew by a further\n15", "per cent this quarter and we expect the same next year.")
    assert docs.find_quote(doc, "Deposits grew by a further 15 per cent this quarter") == 1
    assert docs.find_quote(doc, "Deposits grew by a further per cent this quarter") is None


def test_quotes_within_one_page_are_unaffected():
    assert docs.find_quote(DOC, "We expect deposit growth to stay ahead of loans over the next year.", 2) == 2


# ---------- extraction ----------

CALL = {"quarter": "Q1 FY27", "label": "Jul 2026", "transcript": "u"}
GOOD = {"metric": "other", "statement": "We expect deposit growth to stay ahead of loans over the next year.", "page": "2"}


def _extract(monkeypatch, raw):
    monkeypatch.setattr(transcripts.docs, "pages", lambda url: DOC)
    monkeypatch.setattr(transcripts, "chat_json", lambda *a, **k: raw)
    return transcripts.extract(CALL, 4)


def test_wrong_shaped_items_are_skipped_and_recorded_not_fatal(monkeypatch):
    out = _extract(monkeypatch, {
        "guidance": ["deposit growth will improve",                                        # a bare string
                     dict(GOOD),
                     {"statement": "We expect deposits to double over the next year.", "page": 2},   # not in the text
                     {"statement": "We have spent a large part of the month of June in completing", "page": 1}],  # past
        "business": "A private-sector bank.",
        "analyst_focus": ["margins", {"topic": "margins", "quote": "Will margins expand next year?", "page": 3}]})
    assert [g["id"] for g in out["guidance"]] == ["G4.2"] and out["guidance"][0]["page"] == 2
    assert [(r["id"], r["reason"]) for r in out["rejected"]] == [
        ("G4.1", "malformed"), ("G4.3", "not_verbatim"), ("G4.4", "not_forward_looking")]
    assert out["dropped_unverified"] == 3
    assert out["business"] == {"summary": "A private-sector bank.", "segments": []}
    assert [f["quote"] for f in out["analyst_focus"]] == ["Will margins expand next year?"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("raw", ["Sorry, I cannot read this transcript.", None, 42])
def test_an_answer_that_is_not_an_object_yields_no_guidance_instead_of_crashing(monkeypatch, raw):
    out = _extract(monkeypatch, raw)
    assert out["guidance"] == [] and out["rejected"] == [] and out["business"] is None


def test_a_bare_list_answer_is_read_as_the_guidance_items(monkeypatch):
    out = _extract(monkeypatch, [dict(GOOD)])
    assert [g["statement"] for g in out["guidance"]] == [GOOD["statement"]]


def test_an_analyst_question_is_recorded_as_not_management(monkeypatch):
    out = _extract(monkeypatch, {"guidance": [{"statement": "Will margins expand next year?", "page": 3}]})
    assert out["guidance"] == [] and out["dropped_not_management"] == 1
    assert out["rejected"][0]["reason"] == "not_management" and out["rejected"][0]["speaker"] == "Rahul Jain"


def test_extract_all_keeps_other_calls_when_one_fails(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(transcripts, "pick", lambda c, n: [{**CALL, "quarter": q} for q in ("Q1 FY27", "Q4 FY26")])

    def extract(call, idx):
        if call["quarter"] == "Q4 FY26":
            raise RuntimeError("unreadable")
        return {"call": call["quarter"], "guidance": [GOOD]}

    monkeypatch.setattr(transcripts, "extract", extract)
    out = transcripts.extract_all([], 2)
    assert [c["call"] for c in out] == ["Q1 FY27", "Q4 FY26"] and out[1]["error"] == "unreadable"

```

## 1. Bull 2 cites a number that isn't a cited figure
> "PAT rose 5.7% QoQ and 5.6% YoY, while pre‑provision margin stayed above 25%."

The cited figures are 25.4% and 26.1%. "Above 25%" is true, but 25 is not a reported figure. The thesis builder had already marked the point `grounded: false`, which the app shows as "⚠ unverified". However, `_verify` never acted on that flag, so the second-model check passed the point as verified.

**Fix:**

- If the rewrite still has the number, `repair_point(..., grounded=False)` drops the secondary clause that holds it, along with the cited facts the kept text no longer quotes. It never rewords or substitutes a number.
- If the uncited number is in the main clause, or no figure-based claim would remain, the point stays disputed.
- After a repair, `_verify` sets `grounded` again only if every remaining number is a cited figure.

- the model extracted far fewer candidates this time (about 14, against about 44 before);
- the Q4 FY26 call failed entirely with `'str' object has no attribute 'get'`.

Two defects found:
- **Quotes across page breaks could never verify.** `find_quote` joins page *i* with page *i*+1 so a quote may span the break, but HDFCBANK's running header sat between the two halves. None of the 31 mid-sentence breaks across the five calls could match. Header and footer lines are now dropped **only at the break**:
  - a header line is the same line on at least half the pages (minimum 3);
  - a `Speaker:` label never counts;
  - "Page N of M" lines are also dropped.

  The match is still normalised and verbatim.
- **Wrong-shaped model output lost a whole call.** `extract()` now skips string items, bare string or list answers, and string business or segment values, instead of failing the call. Each rejected item is recorded under `guidance.calls[].rejected` with its id and reason (`malformed`, `not_verbatim`, `not_forward_looking` or `not_management`), so future drops can be explained.

`validate_memo.quote_ok` uses the same page window.

Written for: you, reviewing PR #11 before you decide whether to merge.

I fixed bull 2 and found two defects in how transcript quotes are verified and extracted. The PR is open but not merged or deployed. The full backend suite passes: **325 tests**, the earlier 302 plus 23 new ones that fail without the fix. I made no production requests, rebuilt nothing and changed no data.

- **Branch:** `fix/hdfcbank-qa-grounding-and-transcripts`, created from `origin/main` (`96e7cc8`)
- **Commit:** `72d7e53`
- **PR:** https://github.com/Prateechit/FINN-Financial-Investment-Agent/pull/11

## 1. Bull 2: "stayed above 25%"
**Cause:** the memo already marks bull 2 `grounded: false`, and the app shows "⚠ unverified" on it. But the verification step never acted on that flag, so the second-model check marked the point verified. The validator's failure comes from that same flag.

**Fix:**
- A `grounded: false` point is now flagged, with the uncited number named: "Quotes 25, which is not among its cited figures (5.6, 5.7, 25.4, 26.1)…".
- That sends it through the existing single rewrite.
- If the rewrite repeats the number, the deterministic repair drops only the secondary clause holding it, plus the cited facts the remaining sentence no longer uses. It never rewords or swaps a number.
- If the uncited number is in the main clause, the point stays disputed.

**On the production text:** the point becomes "**PAT rose 5.7% QoQ and 5.6% YoY.**", citing `calc.Q.pat_qoq.Sep 2026` and `X.pat_yoy.Q2 FY27`. None of the other five points is flagged.

**Validator on the downloaded memo:** 1 hard failure as it stands. With the repair applied to a local copy: **no hard failures**, and quotes 4/4.

## 2. Promise Ledger shrinking from 7 rows to 4
**The 10 dropped quotes are not the main cause.**

| Call | Before (kept / dropped) | Now (kept / dropped) |
|---|---|---|
| Q2 FY27 (G5) | 5 / 3 | 1 / 1 |
| Q1 FY27 (G4) | 7 / 5 | 0 / 6 |
| **Q4 FY26 (G3)** | 5 / 4 | **whole call lost:** `'str' object has no attribute 'get'` |
| Q3 FY26 (G2) | 5 / 1 | 1 / 0 |
| Q2 FY26 (G1) | 6 / 3 | 2 / 3 |
| **Total** | **28 / 16** | **4 / 10** |

This time the model proposed about 14 candidate quotes instead of about 44, and one transcript crashed. Dropping 10 of 14 is in line with the 16 dropped before.

**The 10 dropped quotes:** **G5.2, G4.1–G4.6, G1.1, G1.2, G1.4.** I worked these out from the gaps in the kept IDs.

**Their text and the reason for each drop can't be determined.**
- Only counts were stored, and "discarded" covers three cases: not verbatim, not forward-looking, and spoken by an analyst.
- The model's raw answers exist only in the production LLM cache, which I didn't read.
- So I can't say which of the 10 are recoverable. **None are recovered in this PR.**

What I could establish from the five transcripts (downloaded offline from the public BSE links, with a scratch cache):

| Finding | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Quotes crossing a page break can never verify.** Every body page starts with a running header ("HDFC Bank Limited / date / Page N of M / Classification - …"). The code joins a page with the next to allow page-spanning quotes, but the header ends up in the middle. | **False rejection, confirmed.** All 31 mid-sentence page breaks were affected; any of the 10 that crossed one was wrongly rejected. Fixed: header lines (the same line on at least half the pages, never a "Speaker:" label, plus "Page N of M") are dropped only at the break. Now 31/31 such quotes verify, 0 of 65 non-adjacent word sequences falsely match, and the old 28/28 and new 4/4 quotes still verify on the same page. |
| Ligatures, soft hyphens, special spaces, line-end hyphenation | **Not a cause.** None are present; the line-end hyphens are real compound words, which the normaliser already handles. |
| Page references | **Consistent.** All 32 stored quotes verify on the page they cite. |
| Q4 FY26 crash | **A bug, fixed.** A wrong-shaped model answer (a string where an object belonged) discarded the whole call. Those parts are now skipped and recorded. I can't tell which shape it was without the cached answer. |
| Recording why quotes were dropped | **Added.** Each rejected quote is now stored with its ID and reason (malformed, not verbatim, not forward-looking, or not management), so the next rebuild will show exactly why each one was dropped. |

Verbatim matching is no stricter or looser: it is still normalised and exact, and a changed word still fails. No verdict logic changed.

## Tests
- **New:** 8 grounding tests, including a full pipeline run of the bull 2 rewrite and repair, and 15 transcript tests covering page breaks, rejection of non-verbatim quotes and each wrong-shaped answer.
- **Results:** `tests/test_narrative.py` and `tests/test_transcripts.py` together: 140 passed. Full backend suite: **325 passed**.

## Diff review
- 6 files changed: `narrative.py`, `research.py`, `transcripts.py`, `docs.py`, `test_narrative.py`, `validate_memo.py`, plus the new `test_transcripts.py`.
- Nothing touches DIXON or TATATECH data, the frontend or the screenshots, and whitespace is clean.
- **Two side effects to know about:**

## 2. Thesis points
| Point | Grounded | Status | Text |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bull 1 | ✅ | Verified | Revenue growth accelerated to 9.4% YoY in Sep 2026, up from 2.4% in Dec 2025. |
| **Bull 2** | ✅ | **⚠ Disputed** | Q2 FY27 PAT grew 5.6% YoY to ₹20,700 Cr, outpacing the 5-year PAT CAGR of 20.0% — spans the FY24 step-change: assets +59%, likely inorganic. |
| Bull 3 | ✅ | Verified | Management guides for an upward net interest margin trajectory starting from Q3 FY27. |
| Bear 1 | ✅ | Verified | ROA declined to 1.7% in FY26 from 2.0% in FY24, with the promise ledger marking it at risk. |
| Bear 2 | ✅ | Verified | Asset growth slowed to 11.7% in FY26, significantly below the 19.2% recorded in FY23. |
| Bear 3 | ✅ | Verified | Pre-provision margin compressed to 25.4% in Q2 FY27 from 26.1% in Q2 FY26. |
| Watch | — | Unchecked (by design) | Whether Q3 FY27 net interest margin rises, validating the promised upward trajectory. |

**So: 5 verified, 1 disputed, 0 unchecked.**

## 3. Bull 2
- ✅ **No "25%" figure.** This is a new draft from the AI model; the deterministic grounding repair was never needed this time.
- ⚠ **It is disputed:** the second-model check objected "5.6% growth does not outpace 20.0% CAGR". That is right, the comparison is wrong. No deterministic repair fits this kind of error, so the point stays marked "⚠ disputed by FINN's check" in the app. Nothing is hidden.
- ⚠ **₹20,700 Cr is not among its own cited figures.** The pipeline counts it as grounded because it matches a figure somewhere in the full evidence, but neither of the point's two references contains it. The standardised-statements PAT for Sep 2026 is ₹21,537 Cr; I haven't checked whether 20,700 is the exchange-filing figure.

## 4. Guidance quotes
- **Verbatim:** **7/7** on their cited pages, confirmed both by FINN's matcher and by the independent validator.
- **Page breaks:** ✅ **G4.5** (Q1 FY27, p8: "you will see a very handsome, or that's the endeavor to ensure that we are reasonably strong and significant market share…") crosses a page break. It **matches with the new window and would have failed with the old page join**. This is the PR #11 fix working end to end in production.
- **Calls:** all 5 transcripts were read. **Q4 FY26 no longer crashes:** it produced 2 kept quotes and 1 rejected.

## 5. Promise Ledger and rejections
**Ledger: 6 rows** (4 before this rebuild, 7 originally): **2 at risk** (growth trajectory, ROA) and **4 unverifiable** (NIM, MSME, FCNR deposits, home loans).

**The 10 rejected quotes, now with reasons:**
| ID | Reason recorded | My check against the transcript |
|---|---|---|
| G5.2, G4.1, G4.6, G3.2, G1.1, G1.2, G1.4 | `not_management` (credited to analysts Ankit Bihani, Suresh Ganapathy, Abhishek Murarka, Kunal Shah and Mahrukh Adajania) | ❌ **False rejections.** In all 7, the nearest speaker label before the quote is **Srinivasan Vaidyanathan** (the CFO). His labels are inline ("Srinivasan Vaidyanathan: So first is the LCR question. Yes, we would like to operate between 110 and 120…"), and `speaker_at` only recognises labels on their own line, so it credits his answers to the previous analyst. The bug predates PR #11; the new rejection log is what exposed it. |
| G4.2, G4.3 | `not_forward_looking` | **Correct under the current rule.** The wording has none of the forward-looking keywords. |
| G4.4 | `not_verbatim` | **A genuine mismatch.** The model wrote "endeavo**u**r" and the transcript says "endeavor". Accepting it would mean loosening the verbatim rule. |

**7 of the 10 drops are recoverable:** they are verbatim, forward-looking statements by management. Recovering them needs a code fix to `speaker_at` (recognise inline `Name: text` labels), which this task didn't allow.

cat > ~/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/3d6517633a89a6f0/c363bd54-6dbf-4695-9f84-97a9ce39aca0/scratchpad/final/new_section.py <<'PYEOF'
# ---------- every figure is a cited figure ----------

def _cited_text(evidence: list[dict]) -> str:
    """The numbers a point may quote: its cited figures (and the figures a cited signal is computed from) with their
    labels — a caveat such as "assets +59%" comes from one — and the words of its cited signals, guidance and ledger
    rows. Nothing outside the point's own references counts."""
    parts = [f"{f['value']} {f.get('label') or ''}" for f in _figures(evidence)]
    for e in evidence:
        parts += [str(e[k]) for k in ("text", "statement", "target", "quote", "promise", "delivered", "why") if e.get(k)]
    return " ".join(parts)


def cited_grounded(point: str, evidence: list[dict]) -> bool:
    """Every number in the point is in its own cited evidence (± rounding) — what the thesis's `grounded` flag asks.
    A figure that appears elsewhere in the memo but in none of the point's references does not count."""
    return not ungrounded(point, _cited_text(evidence))


def grounding_issue(p: dict) -> str | None:
    """A point the thesis builder marked ungrounded (a number not in its own cited evidence): "pre-provision margin
    stayed above 25%" cites 25.4% and 26.1% — true, but 25 is not a reported figure."""
    if p.get("grounded") is not False:
        return None
    ev = p.get("evidence") or []
    bad = ungrounded(p["point"], _cited_text(ev))
    if not bad:
        return "Cites no evidence." if not p.get("refs") else None
    cited = ", ".join(f"{v:g}" for v in sorted({abs(float(f['value'])) for f in _figures(ev)})) or "none"
    return (f"Quotes {', '.join(f'{n:g}' for n in bad)}, which is not among its cited figures ({cited}); quote a cited "
            f"figure or drop that claim.")


def _caveats(point: str, evidence: list[dict]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The caveat thesis.build appends from a cited fact's label (" — spans the FY24 step-change: …"), by fact id."""
    out = {}

# ---------- every figure is a cited figure ----------

def _cited_text(evidence: list[dict]) -> str:
    """The numbers a point may quote: its cited figures (and the figures a cited signal is computed from) with their
    labels — a caveat such as "assets +59%" comes from one — and the words of its cited signals, guidance and ledger
    rows. Nothing outside the point's own references counts."""
    parts = [f"{f['value']} {f.get('label') or ''}" for f in _figures(evidence)]
    for e in evidence:
        parts += [str(e[k]) for k in ("text", "statement", "target", "quote", "promise", "delivered", "why") if e.get(k)]
    return " ".join(parts)


def cited_grounded(point: str, evidence: list[dict]) -> bool:
    """Every number in the point is in its own cited evidence (± rounding) — what the thesis's `grounded` flag asks.
    A figure that appears elsewhere in the memo but in none of the point's references does not count."""
    return not ungrounded(point, _cited_text(evidence))


def grounding_issue(p: dict) -> str | None:
    """A point the thesis builder marked ungrounded (a number not in its own cited evidence): "pre-provision margin
    stayed above 25%" cites 25.4% and 26.1% — true, but 25 is not a reported figure."""
    if p.get("grounded") is not False:
        return None
    ev = p.get("evidence") or []
    bad = ungrounded(p["point"], _cited_text(ev))
    if not bad:
        return "Cites no evidence." if not p.get("refs") else None
    cited = ", ".join(f"{v:g}" for v in sorted({abs(float(f['value'])) for f in _figures(ev)})) or "none"
    return (f"Quotes {', '.join(f'{n:g}' for n in bad)}, which is not among its cited figures ({cited}); quote a cited "
            f"figure or drop that claim.")


def _caveats(point: str, evidence: list[dict]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The caveat thesis.build appends from a cited fact's label (" — spans the FY24 step-change: …"), by fact id."""
    out = {}
    for e in evidence:
        label = str(e.get("label") or "")
        if e.get("type") == "fact" and "(" in label:
            caveat = f" — {label[label.index('(') + 1:].rstrip(')')}"
            if caveat in point:
                out[e["id"]] = caveat
    return out


def _without_clauses(point: str, refs: list[str], evidence: list[dict], drop) -> tuple[str, list[str], list[dict]] | None:
    """Drop the secondary clauses `drop(clause)` selects — never the main one — then the cited facts whose figure the
    kept text no longer quotes, with any caveat such a fact carried (signals, guidance and ledger references stay).
    Nothing is reworded. None if no figure-based claim would remain."""
    caveats = _caveats(point, evidence)
    body = point
    for c in caveats.values():
        body = body.replace(c, "")
    body = body.strip().rstrip(".")
    seps = list(_CLAUSE_SEP.finditer(body))
    starts = [0] + [s.end() for s in seps]
    ends = [s.start() for s in seps] + [len(body)]
    clauses = [body[a:b] for a, b in zip(starts, ends)]
    kept = clauses[0] + "".join(seps[k - 1].group() + c for k, c in enumerate(clauses[1:], 1) if not drop(c))
    kept = kept.strip().rstrip(".,;")
    if not re.search(r"\d", kept):
        return None
    quoted = numbers(kept)
    if len(refs) == len(evidence):
        pairs = [(r, e) for r, e in zip(refs, evidence)
                 if e.get("type") != "fact" or any(abs(abs(q) - abs(float(e["value"]))) <= 0.051 for q in quoted)]
        if pairs:
            refs, evidence = [r for r, _ in pairs], [e for _, e in pairs]
    still = {e.get("id") for e in evidence}
    return kept + "".join(c for fid, c in caveats.items() if fid in still) + ".", refs, evidence


# A level stated beside a cited rate — "grew 5.6% YoY to ₹20,700 Cr" — as its own phrase.
_AMOUNT = re.compile(r"\s+(?:to|at|of)\s+(?:₹|Rs\.?|INR)\s?[\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?\s*(?:cr|crore|bn|billion|mn|million|lakh)\b",
                     re.I)


def trim_ungrounded_clause(point: str, refs: list[str], evidence: list[dict]) -> tuple[str, list[str], list[dict]] | None:
    """Last resort for a point that, after its rewrite, still quotes a number not in its own cited evidence: drop a
    "to ₹N Cr" phrase stating an uncited level, and each secondary clause quoting an uncited number ("…, while
    pre-provision margin stayed above 25%"), when the rest is a figure-based claim whose every number is cited. Nothing
    is reworded or substituted. None when the main claim itself rests on the uncited number."""
    text = _cited_text(evidence)
    if not ungrounded(point, text):
        return None
    for m in reversed(list(_AMOUNT.finditer(point))):
        if ungrounded(m.group(), text):
            point = point[:m.start()] + point[m.end():]
    cut = _without_clauses(point, refs, evidence, lambda c: bool(ungrounded(c, text)))
    if not cut or ungrounded(cut[0], text):
        return None
    return cut


# ---------- a comparison says what its figures show ----------

_AHEAD = re.compile(r"\b(?:outpac\w*|outgr[eo]w\w*|outstrip\w*|exceed\w*|surpass\w*|ahead\s+of|faster\s+than|"
                    r"beat(?:s|ing)?)\b(?P<by>\s+by\b)?", re.I)
_BEHIND = re.compile(r"\b(?:lag(?:s|ged|ging)?|trail\w*|behind|slower\s+than)\b", re.I)
_PCT_FIG = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.])(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s?%")


def _rate_kind(value: float, evidence: list[dict]) -> str | None:
    for f in _figures(evidence):
        if round(abs(float(f["value"])), 2) == round(value, 2):
            fid = str(f.get("id") or "")
            if "cagr" in fid.lower() or "cagr" in str(f.get("label") or "").lower():
                return "multi-year CAGR"
            kind = _metric(fid)[1] if "." in fid else None
            if kind:
                return {"qoq": "quarter-on-quarter", "yoy": "year-on-year"}[kind]
    return None


def _comparison_word(text: str):
    """The first "outpacing" / "lagging"-type word in the text, and whether it says the first figure is ahead."""
    found = [(m.start(), m, rx is _AHEAD and not m.group("by")) for rx in (_AHEAD, _BEHIND) for m in rx.finditer(text)]
    return min(found, key=lambda x: x[0])[1:] if found else (None, None)


def _comparisons(point: str) -> list[tuple]:
    """(word, figure before it, figure after it, claims the first is ahead) for "A% … outpacing … B%"."""
    out = []
    for rx in (_AHEAD, _BEHIND):
        for m in rx.finditer(point):
            before = [x for x in _PCT_FIG.finditer(point) if x.end() <= m.start()]
            after = _PCT_FIG.search(point, m.end())
            if before and after:
                ahead = rx is _AHEAD and not m.group("by")      # "outpaced by" says the first is behind
                out.append((m.start(), m.group().strip(), float(before[-1].group(1)), float(after.group(1)), ahead))
    return [x[1:] for x in sorted(out, key=lambda x: x[0])]


def comparison_direction_issue(point: str, evidence: list[dict]) -> str | None:
    """A comparison must point the way its figures do, between like-for-like rates: "PAT grew 5.6% YoY, outpacing the
    5-year PAT CAGR of 20.0%" says the smaller figure is ahead; a quarter-on-quarter rate is not set against an
    annual one."""
    for word, a, b, ahead in _comparisons(point):
        if (ahead and a < b) or (not ahead and a > b):
            return (f"Says {a:g}% {'is ahead of' if ahead else 'trails'} {b:g}% (\"{word}\"), but {a:g}% is the "
                    f"{'smaller' if ahead else 'larger'} figure; state what the figures show or drop the comparison.")
        ka, kb = _rate_kind(a, evidence), _rate_kind(b, evidence)
        if ka and kb and ka != kb and "quarter-on-quarter" in (ka, kb):
            return f"Compares a {ka} rate ({a:g}%) with a {kb} rate ({b:g}%) — not like-for-like."
    return None


def trim_bad_comparison(point: str, refs: list[str], evidence: list[dict]) -> tuple[str, list[str], list[dict]] | None:
    """Last resort for a comparison that contradicts its figures or is not like-for-like: drop the secondary clause
    that opens with it ("…, outpacing the 5-year PAT CAGR of 20.0%") and the facts only it quoted. None when the
    comparison sits in the main clause."""
    if not comparison_direction_issue(point, evidence):
        return None

    def opens_comparison(clause: str) -> bool:
        m, _ = _comparison_word(clause)
        return bool(m) and not _PCT_FIG.search(clause, 0, m.start()) and bool(_PCT_FIG.search(clause, m.end()))

    cut = _without_clauses(point, refs, evidence, opens_comparison)
    if not cut or cut[0].rstrip(".") == point.rstrip(".") or comparison_direction_issue(cut[0], cut[2]):
        return None
    return cut

                                                   LATEST, grounded=False)
    assert point == "Q2 FY27 PAT grew 5.6% YoY."                      # nothing invented: only cited text is kept
    assert refs == ["X.pat_yoy.Q2 FY27"] and [e["id"] for e in evidence] == refs
    th = {"bull": [{"point": point, "refs": refs, "evidence": evidence, "grounded": True}], "bear": []}
    assert narrative.thesis_issues(th, {"rows": []}, LATEST) == {}

Written for: you, reviewing PR #12 before you decide whether to merge.

All three issues are fixed and the PR is open. It is not merged or deployed. The full backend suite passes: **347 tests**, the earlier 325 plus 22 new ones. I made no production requests, rebuilt nothing and changed no data. To count which new tests fail without the fix, I temporarily restored the old source files; they are back to the committed versions and the working tree is clean.

- **Branch:** `fix/speaker-comparison-cited-grounding`, created from `origin/main` (`5729d7e`)
- **Commit:** `9a1d2f9`
- **PR:** https://github.com/Prateechit/FINN-Financial-Investment-Agent/pull/12

## 1. Speaker attribution
`speaker_at` (in `backend/finn/pull/transcripts.py`) only recognised a speaker label on its own line. It now also recognises labels at the start of an answer ("Srinivasan Vaidyanathan: So first is the LCR question…"), under the same rules as before:
- a label counts only if it recurs, is the Moderator, or is an analyst the moderator introduced;
- every word of an inline label must start with a capital, so "The answer is: yes" isn't a label;
- a one-off cover heading ("MANAGEMENT: MR. …") doesn't count.

Checked against the real HDFCBANK transcripts:
- **All 7 false rejections** (G5.2, G4.1, G4.6, G3.2, G1.1, G1.2, G1.4) are now credited to **Srinivasan Vaidyanathan**. Each is verbatim on its page and forward-looking, so a rebuild would keep them.
- All 11 distinct analyst questions are still credited to analysts.
- None of the 35 previously kept management quotes changes. Verbatim matching itself is unchanged.

## 2. Bull 2's comparison
- **New check:** flags "outpacing / exceeding / ahead of / beating" or "lagging / trailing" when the figures say the opposite ("outpaced by" reverses the direction). It also flags a quarter-on-quarter rate set against a year-on-year rate or a multi-year CAGR.
- **Effect:** a flagged point goes through the usual single rewrite. If the rewrite still has the problem, the repair drops the clause that makes the comparison, along with the facts and the caveat only that clause used. If the comparison is the main claim, the point stays disputed.
- **Prompt:** the thesis prompt now states the rule.

## 3. Bull 2's ₹20,700 Cr
- **Grounding:** a point now counts as grounded only if every number is in **its own cited evidence**: cited figures and their labels, signal text, guidance and ledger rows. Ledger evidence now includes the reported outcome text as well.
- **Repair:** it may drop a "to ₹N Cr" phrase whose figure isn't cited. It never substitutes a figure.
- **Validator:** it now re-checks grounding against each point's own evidence instead of trusting the memo's flag, and it independently catches the ₹20,700 Cr.

**Bull 2 after the fix:** "Q2 FY27 PAT grew 5.6% YoY to ₹20,700 Cr, outpacing the 5-year PAT CAGR of 20.0% — spans the FY24 step-change…" → "**Q2 FY27 PAT grew 5.6% YoY.**", citing `X.pat_yoy.Q2 FY27`.

## Tests and offline replay
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New tests | 22: speaker labels, comparison direction, grounding (including a figure that appears elsewhere in the memo not counting) and a full pipeline run. **20 of 22 fail** without the fix; the 2 that pass are speaker-label controls the old code already handled. |
| Changed test | One test from the previous PR (#11), changed because an uncited "to ₹N Cr" phrase is now trimmed on purpose. |
| Backend suite | **347 passed**. The frontend build was skipped because no frontend files changed. |
| Replay of the new checks | 48 points across DIXON, TATATECH, three HDFCBANK snapshots and the test fixtures. Only the two known-bad bull 2 versions are flagged; **no false positives**. |
| Validator | DIXON 52/52 quotes, no failures. TATATECH 16/16, none. HDFCBANK 07:51 28/28, none. HDFCBANK 19:10: 1 failure ("25%"). HDFCBANK 19:34: 1 failure (₹20,700, now caught). HDFCBANK 19:34 with the repair applied: **none**. |

## Remaining limitations
- **Production is unchanged.** Bull 2 is still disputed in the live memo, and the 7 quotes stay rejected until you merge, deploy and approve an HDFCBANK rebuild.
- **A rebuild re-asks the AI models,** so the new draft can contain different problems. The checks and repairs cover these three kinds.
- **The comparison check is narrow.** It catches explicit comparison words between two percentage figures, not looser wording such as "well above" or "higher than".
- **More rewrites.** The stricter grounding may send more points through one extra rewrite, costing a few more model calls. The replay showed no false positives.
- **Thinner text.** A repaired point can be much shorter ("Q2 FY27 PAT grew 5.6% YoY."): correct but less informative.
- **The README screenshots** of the HDFCBANK memo are still out of date.

# FINN — Financial Investment Agent
**Project Submission | ENAM Holdings AI Engineer Build Challenge**

Dear ENAM Holdings Team,

I am pleased to submit **FINN (Financial Investment Agent)**, an AI-powered financial research assistant designed to make investment intelligence more accessible, structured and actionable.

Traditional investment research requires investors to continuously monitor company announcements, financial statements, market movements and management commentary across multiple sources. FINN addresses this challenge through two complementary modes:

**1. Push Intelligence:** Continuously monitors a curated portfolio of Indian listed companies, identifies potentially material corporate developments, detects relevant price and volume anomalies, and presents concise, contextual explanations.

**2. Pull Research:** Enables on-demand company research through structured financial analysis, historical performance trends, management guidance versus actual outcomes, a Promise Ledger, and evidence-backed bull and bear investment cases.

FINN combines financial data pipelines, AI-powered information extraction, evidence-grounded analysis and verification mechanisms to create a unified research workflow.

The application is built with a FastAPI/Python backend and a React-based mobile-first Progressive Web App. It integrates public market and corporate information sources and uses PostgreSQL for persistent data storage.

A key design principle is that **investment narratives should remain accountable to numbers and primary evidence**. FINN therefore incorporates source citations, transcript quote verification, period consistency checks and evidence-grounding validation.

**Project links**

- Live application: https://finn-financial-investment-agent-eosin.vercel.app/
- GitHub repository: https://github.com/Prateechit/FINN-Financial-Investment-Agent
- Backend API: https://finn-api-bbyo.onrender.com/

The project has been developed as a working, deployed prototype, with emphasis on practical usability, reliability, traceability and scalable architecture.

Thank you for the opportunity to participate. I look forward to presenting FINN and explaining its architecture, implementation decisions and potential applications.

# FINN — AI-Assisted Build History

**FINN (Financial Investment Agent)** · ENAM Holdings AI Engineer Build Challenge

This document records how FINN was built: what was built in each phase, which AI tools were used, and which steps were taken by the AI assistant and which by the project owner. Every statement is drawn from the Git history, the GitHub pull-request records, the project's decision log (`docs/DECISIONS.md`) or the Claude Code session transcript. Where the record does not settle a point, the document says so.

| | |
|---|---|
| Build window | 9 – 12 November 2026 |
| Commits on `main` | 35: 23 authored commits and 12 pull-request merges |
| Pull requests | 12, all merged into `main` by the repository owner |
| Backend tests | 0 → 28 → 112 → 299 → **347** (collected at each milestone; see [§6](#6-testing-milestones)) |
| AI coding tool | Claude Code, running the Claude Opus 5.5 model |
| Production | Vercel (frontend) · Render (API) · Neon Postgres (database) · GitHub Actions (scheduled ingest) |

Commit times are IST (UTC+5:30), as Git records them. Production and server events are UTC, as the FINN API reports them.

---

## 1. AI tools used

| Tool | Role | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Claude Code**, Anthropic's coding agent, run in the VS Code extension | Wrote the code, tests, scripts and documentation; ran tests, audits and read-only production checks; prepared commits and branches | Session `c363bd54-6dbf-4695-9f84-97a9ce39aca0`, exported to `docs/ai-history/` by `scripts/export_history.py`. All **23 of 23** authored commits carry `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5`. PRs #10–#12 end with "Generated with Claude Code". |
| **Claude Opus 5.5** (`claude-opus-5-5`) | The model behind every assistant turn in the session | The session transcript records `claude-opus-5-5` on all 2,551 assistant messages. |

**No other AI coding tool** (for example Copilot, Cursor, ChatGPT or Codex) is named anywhere in the repository or the session record, so none is claimed here.

**Models inside the product are separate.** FINN itself calls the free tiers of **Google Gemini** and **Groq** (`gpt-oss-120b`, `gpt-oss-20b`, `qwen3.8-27b`) at runtime, with **Ollama** (`gemma3:4b`) as a local development fallback. These are components of the product, not tools used to build it (`backend/finn/llm.py`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`).

---

## 2. Who did what

The session record shows a consistent division of work. The project owner set direction and constraints, controlled anything outward-facing, and merged every PR. The assistant implemented, tested, verified and reported, and asked for approval before any production action.

| Activity | Project owner | Claude Code (AI) |
|---|---|---|
| Product brief and scope | Wrote the opening brief (Push and Pull workflows, 15–20 stock portfolio, ENAM requirements) and approved the proposed plan | Proposed the architecture and plan; ran the data-source checks (`spikes/`) |
| Implementation | Set constraints in each request (for example "Do not push or deploy", "Do not rebuild any memo", "Do not expose secrets") | Wrote all application code, tests, scripts and documentation |
| Hosting accounts and secrets | Set up the Vercel, Render and Neon services; entered secrets in the Render dashboard and in GitHub Actions; confirmed deployments from the Render dashboard | Wrote the deploy configuration (`render.yaml`, `vercel.json`) and the migration script; checked deployments with read-only requests only |
| Pushes to `main` | Gave explicit instructions for each early push to `main` and for the fast-forward of `edc3910` ("I approve merging commit `edc3910` … into `main`") | Ran those pushes. After that, pushed feature branches only |
| Pull requests | Opened PRs #1–#9 on GitHub; **reviewed and merged all 12** | Opened PRs #10–#12 with the `gh` CLI. **Ran no merge command in the session record** |
| Code review | Asked for reviews at set points (for example "read-only code review of PR #1") and chose which findings to fix | Carried out the requested reviews and reported findings before changing code |
| Production memo rebuilds | **Approved each rebuild individually**, usually as "exactly one POST", after confirming the deployed commit | Sent exactly the approved request, polled with GET only, never retried, and reported the outcome, including failures |
| Ingestion workflow | Configured the GitHub secrets; triggered the manual run (#3) | Diagnosed the problem read-only (missing secrets; scheduled runs delayed or dropped); verified the effect with GET requests |
| Decisions on remaining issues | Chose what to fix and what to leave (for example kept one known verifier quirk unchanged) | Reported what remained open, with evidence |

The record does not show how much time the owner spent reviewing each PR on GitHub. It shows only that every merge was made from the owner's account (`mergedBy: Prateechit`) and that the assistant never ran a merge.

---

## 3. Development timeline

### Phase 0 — Data-source checks (9 Nov)
The first files written were throw-away scripts in `spikes/`, which tested each candidate source before any design was fixed. Results are in `docs/DECISIONS.md`:
- **Prices:** yfinance as the primary source, with the NSE bhavcopy as fallback.
- **Announcements:** NSE corporate announcements as the primary source, with BSE as fallback.
- **Results:** NSE Integrated Filing XBRL for current results, because the older XBRL endpoint ends in Dec 2024.
- **Financials and documents:** screener.in for statements and for discovering transcripts.
- **Transcripts:** a test transcript was about 16k tokens, so a whole transcript fits in one model call and the Promise Ledger needs no retrieval step (no RAG).

### Phase 1 — Core system (9 Nov, 18:03–18:33 IST)
| Commit | What was built |
|---|---|
| `f84abb6` | Push pipeline: NSE, screener and yfinance sources; XBRL results engine; rule-based classifier; explainable materiality scoring |
| `b48f912` | Pull pipeline: deterministic financials, quote-verified guidance extraction, Promise Ledger, bull/bear thesis; FastAPI layer; story clustering; penalty-vs-revenue materiality |
| `f93bd55` | Mobile PWA frontend (Brief, Alerts, Research memo, Portfolio, Company); deploy configuration; evidence guards; AI-history export |

**Decisions recorded at this point:**
- the AI models never produce numbers: every figure comes from code;
- every quote must be found verbatim on its cited page;
- everything is cached by content hash;
- a static Vite + React PWA was chosen over Next.js.

### Phase 2 — Validation on real companies with real models (9 Nov, 19:12–20:18 IST)
| Commit | What changed, and what found it |
|---|---|
| `55d3f72` | **First live run, on DIXON.** It exposed lenient verdicts (FY26 capex of ₹1,058 Cr called "delivered" against a ₹1,100–1,200 Cr guide). A deterministic range check now overrides such verdicts. Also added: free-tier model routing and fallback, and new margin and profit signals. |
| `284a5df` | **Second company, HDFC Bank.** Added a lender fact table and a "no proxy metric" guard (NIM cannot be judged from PAT margin). FY24 merger growth is now labelled as a step-change. First smoke test and **28 unit tests**. |
| `7da34e0` | **Groq added.** Introduced the second-model claim verifier, which triggers one rewrite. A speaker-turn check now drops guidance spoken by analysts, and a horizon guard stops "missed" verdicts on open promises. |

**Result recorded in the decision log:** DIXON 52/52 and HDFC Bank 28/28 guidance quotes verbatim, and 6/6 thesis points grounded for each company.

### Phase 3 — Deployment and fiscal-period correctness (9 Nov 22:21 – 10 Nov 01:37 IST)
| Commit | What changed |
|---|---|
| `9932c08` | Moved from SQLite to Neon Postgres; batched price queries. The owner then deployed the API on Render and the PWA on Vercel. |
| `d6088ce` | Company names now resolve to NSE tickers before research starts; fixed a stale search on Enter. |
| `d00f648` | **Fiscal-period alignment:** each promise is judged on figures from the period it is about (Indian fiscal year, Apr–Mar). Tests: 31 → **112**. |
| `edc3910` | Quarterly margin comparisons now use exact margins rather than screener's rounded OPM % (16.03% vs 15.72%, where rounding showed 16% vs 16%). Fast-forwarded into `main` with the owner's written approval. Tests: **131**. |

### Phase 4 — Narrative accountability, through reviewed PRs (10 Nov)
From here on, every change went through a feature branch and a PR merged by the owner. Each fix came from a finding in a real production memo, mostly TATATECH and HDFCBANK.

| PR | Merge | What it fixed | Tests at merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1 | `016a6d6` | Thesis and credibility wording made consistent with fiscal-period evidence; second-pass verification recorded. Two review findings were fixed before merge. | 169 |
| #2 | `5332283` | QoQ and YoY growth figures accepted as comparison evidence (removed a false positive) | 188 |
| #3 | `d41ad7e` | Margin promises get their base-quarter figure; promise-period labels fixed. Six review findings fixed. | 225 |
| #4 | `3408129` | Unmet-promise claims repaired, verifier evidence aligned, and **stale-memo refresh made safe**: at most one build at a time, a cooldown after failures, and a failed rebuild never replaces a good memo | 258 |
| #5 | `d253e69` | Flags cross-series trends, and "failed" claims about promises that were not missed | 281 |
| #6 | `e16d84b` | Deterministic repairs: move a cross-series trend onto one series; give a mislabelled period its real label | 299 |

Between these PRs, the owner approved individual production rebuilds of TATATECH and HDFCBANK. Each rebuild was then audited read-only. The final TATATECH memo (built `2026-11-10T07:29:57`) passed the period audit with 0 failing rows and had 16/16 quotes verbatim.

### Phase 6 — Operational reliability (10 Nov)
These were read-only diagnoses, with no code change:
- **Scheduled ingestion.** Only 2 scheduled runs had happened, and production data had not changed. The likely cause, confirmed once the secrets were set, was that the Actions secrets were missing and the CLI fell back silently to a throwaway SQLite database. The owner configured the secrets and triggered manual run #3. Production announcements then went from **170 to 173**. Delayed or dropped scheduled runs were also documented.
- **Prices.** After ingestion, the latest close was still 9 Nov. The NSE holiday calendar showed **10 Nov was a trading holiday** (Diwali-Balipratipada), so this was expected, not an ingestion fault.

```
# FINN — frontend

The FINN mobile-first PWA: React 19, TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind CSS 4. All data comes from the FINN API. The project overview, the backend setup and the full API reference are in the [root README](../README.md).

Live app: https://finn-financial-investment-agent-eosin.vercel.app

## Run locally

Start the API first (see the root README, *Getting started*), so it listens on `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. Then:

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173 — the dev server proxies /api to http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Vite dev server with hot reload (`host: true`, so you can open it from a phone on the same network) |
| `npm run build` | TypeScript type-check (`tsc -b`) and production build into `dist/` |
| `npm run lint` | oxlint |
| `npm run preview` | Serve the production build locally |

## Configuration

One build-time variable:

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `VITE_API_URL` | Base URL of the API, for example `https://finn-api-bbyo.onrender.com`. Leave it unset in development to use the `/api` proxy. It is baked into the bundle when the app is built. |

## Layout

```
src/
  App.tsx              tab navigation and routing between screens
  screens/             Brief · Alerts · Research · Memo · Portfolio (with the company page) · SettingsSheet
  components/          Story (a Brief story card) · Charts · ui (shared primitives)
  lib/                 api.ts (typed API client and response types) · hooks.ts · format.ts
public/
  manifest.webmanifest, icons, sw.js   PWA manifest and service worker
```

In production builds, the service worker caches the app shell and keeps the last API responses as an offline fallback (`src/main.tsx` registers `public/sw.js`).

## Deployment

The app is deployed on Vercel from the `main` branch with `vercel.json` (Vite framework, output `dist/`, `sw.js` served without caching, hashed assets cached for a year). Set `VITE_API_URL` in the Vercel project's environment variables. The API allows cross-origin requests only from the origins configured in `FINN_CORS_ORIGINS`, so preview deployments need their origin added there before they can reach the API.

```
